children.text: buddho bhagavān kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s> in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>.

children.text: atha sambahulānāṃ kāpilavāstavānāṃ śākyānāṃ saṃsthāgāre saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃrūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, while many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> were seated and assembled in the meeting hall, this sort of conversation arose among them.

children.text: kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇakulavaṃśaś ca ||
children.translated_text: "From where, sirs, have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? What is their foremost origin? What is their lineage? And what is the ancient family line of the <s>Śākyas</s>?"

children.text: sacetkaścid asmākam upasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣām paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti ||
children.translated_text: "If someone were to approach us and ask thus, 'From where, sirs, have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? What is their foremost origin? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family line?'

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭā vayaṃ kiṃ vyākuryāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when asked in this way, what should we answer?

children.text: na ca punar jānīmaḥ kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaśca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti ||
children.translated_text: And furthermore, we do not know from where the <s>Śākyas</s> have arisen, what their foremost origin is, what their lineage is, or what their ancient family line is.

children.text: ete vayaṃ yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let us therefore go to the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavantam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ yathā cāsmākaṃ bhagavān vyākaroti tathainaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, let us ask the Blessed One about this very matter; and just as the Blessed One explains it to us, so shall we remember it."

children.text: atha sambahulāḥ kāpilavāstavāḥ śākyā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ sambahulāḥ kāpilavāstavāḥ śākyā bhagavantam idam avocan ||
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, the many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> said this to the Blessed One.

children.text: ihāsmākam bhadanta sambahulānāṃ kāpilavāstavānāṃ śākyānāṃ saṃsthāgāre saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃrūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Here, venerable sir, while many of us <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> were seated and assembled in the meeting hall, this sort of conversation arose among us.

children.text: kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaśca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'From where have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? What is their foremost origin? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family line?'

children.text: sacet kaścid asmākam upasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaśca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti evaṃ pṛṣṭā vayaṃ kiṃ vyākuryāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If someone were to approach us and ask thus, 'From where, sirs, have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? What is their foremost origin? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family line?' when asked in this way, what should we answer?

children.text: na ca punar jānīmaḥ kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti ||
children.translated_text: And furthermore, we do not know from where the <s>Śākyas</s> have arisen, what their foremost origin is, what their lineage is, or what their ancient family line is.

children.text: ete vayaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkramāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we have approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavantam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, we ask the Blessed One about this very matter.

children.text: yathā cāsmākaṃ bhagavān vyākariṣyati tathainaṃ dhārayiṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: And just as the Blessed One will explain it to us, so shall we remember it."

children.text: te vayam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ kuto bhagavan nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti ||
children.translated_text: "So we ask this very matter: from where, Blessed One, have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? What is their foremost origin? What is their lineage? And what is the ancient family line of the <s>Śākyas</s>?"

children.text: atha bhagavata etad abhavat ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One.

children.text: saced ahaṃ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kuryāṃ sthānam etad vidyate yad anyatīrthikaparivrājakā evaṃ vadeyuḥ ātmaślāghī śramaṇo gautamo yad icchati tad vyākarotīti ||
children.translated_text: "If I were to give a discourse on <s>dharma</s> concerning the ancient family line of the <s>Śākyas</s>, it is possible that wanderers of other sects would say, 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> praises himself; he explains whatever he wishes.'"

children.text: atha ko nu mama śrāvakaḥ pratibalaḥ syād yaḥ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kuryāt tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanastasyām eva pariṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Now which disciple of mine would be capable of giving the monks a discourse on <s>dharma</s> concerning the ancient family line of the <s>Śākyas</s>?" At that very time the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> was seated and assembled in that same gathering.

children.text: bhavati gautamā sa samayo yad ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate saṃvartamāne loke yadbhūyasā sattvā ābhāsvare devanikāye upapadyante te tatra bhavanti rūpiṇo manomayāḥ avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ svayamprabhā vihāyasaṃgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥ prītyāhārāḥ dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: "There comes a time, <s>Gautama</s>, when this world contracts. As the world is contracting, beings for the most part are reborn among the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods. There they are embodied, mind-made, complete, with unimpaired faculties, furnished with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, enduring in appearance, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, sustained by joy, long-lived, and they remain for a long stretch of time.

children.text: tena khalu samayeneyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ekodakā bhavatyekārṇavā ||
children.translated_text: At that time this great earth is a single mass of water, one ocean.

children.text: yaḥ khalu ekodakāyā mahāpṛthivyā ekārṇavāyā upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrchati saṃtanoti tadyathā payasaḥ pakvasya śītībhūtasya upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrchati saṃtanoti
children.translated_text: Over the great earth, which is a single mass of water and one ocean, a film gathers, coagulates, and spreads out by the wind, just as over boiled milk that has cooled a film gathers, coagulates, and spreads out by the wind.

children.text: evam ekodakāyā mahāpṛthivyā ekārṇavāyā upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrchati saṃtanoti ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, over the great earth, which is a single mass of water and one ocean, a film gathers, coagulates, and spreads out by the wind.

children.text: sa bhavati pṛthivīraso varṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampannaḥ evaṃrūpo varṇena tadyathā navanītam evaṃrūpo rasena tadyathā kṣaudramadhv aneḍakam ||
children.translated_text: That becomes the savor of earth, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste: in color it is like fresh butter, and in taste it is like pure bee-honey.

children.text: bhavati gautamā sa samayo yad ayaṃ loko vivartate vivartamāne loke tata eke sattvā āyuḥkṣayāt karmakṣayāt puṇyakṣayāt ābhāsvarād devanikāyāccyutvā ittham āgacchanti mānuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyām ||
children.translated_text: There comes a time, <s>Gautama</s>, when this world expands. As the world is expanding, certain beings, after passing away from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> class of gods through the exhaustion of lifespan, exhaustion of karma, and exhaustion of merit, come here into the condition shared by human beings.

children.text: te iha bhavanti rūpiṇo manomayā avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ svayamprabhā vihāyasaṃgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥ prītyāhārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Here they are embodied, mind-made, complete, with unimpaired faculties, furnished with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, enduring in appearance, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, sustained by joy, long-lived, and they remain for a long stretch of time.

children.text: tena khalu samayena na sūryācandramasor loke prādurbhāvo bhavati na nakṣatrāṇām na kṣaṇalavamuhūrtānām na rātriṃdivasānām na māsārdhamāsṛtusaṃvatsarāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: At that time there is no manifestation in the world of sun and moon, no manifestation of the stars, no moments, instants, or muhūrtas, and no nights and days, months, half-months, seasons, or years.

children.text: na strī prajñāyate na puruṣo nānyatra sattvaḥ sattva iti saṃkhyā gacchati ||
children.translated_text: No woman is perceived, no man, nor any other distinction; it is counted simply as "a being, a being."

children.text: athānyatamo lolupajātīyaḥ sattvaḥ pṛthivīrasam aṅgulyagreṇāsvādayati yathā yathāsvādayati tathā tathā rocayate yathā yathā rocayate tathā tathā kavaḍīkārāhāropakrameṇa paribhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain being of a greedy nature tasted the earth-essence with the tip of a finger. In just the measure that he tasted it, in that measure it pleased him; and in just the measure that it pleased him, in that measure he consumed it by the method of morsel-food.

children.text: adrākṣur anye'pi sattvāstaṃ sattvaṃ pṛthivīrasam aṅgulyagreṇāsvādayamānam yathā yathāsvādayati tathā tathā rocayate yathā yathā rocayate tathā tathā kavaḍīkāropakrameṇa paribhuktavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Other beings too saw that being tasting the earth-essence with the tip of his finger: in just the measure that he tasted it, in that measure it pleased him, and in just the measure that it pleased him, in that measure he had consumed it by the method of morsel-food.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punas te sattvāḥ pṛthivīrasam aṅgulyagreṇa āsvādayitum ārabdhāḥ yathā yathāsvādayanti tathā tathā rocayante yathā yathā rocayante tataḥ kavaḍīkāropakrameṇa paribhuktavantaḥ yataś ca te sattvāḥ pṛthivīrasaṃ kavaḍīkārāhāropakrameṇa paribhuktās tatas teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kharatvaṃ ca gurutvaṃ ca kāye 'vakrāntam ||
children.translated_text: Having seen this, those beings then began to taste the earth-essence with the tip of a finger. In just the measure that they tasted it, in that measure it pleased them; in just the measure that it pleased them, they consumed it by the method of morsel-food. And because those beings consumed the earth-essence by the method of morsel-food, hardness and heaviness entered into their bodies.

children.text: teṣāṃ yāsau śubhā varṇanibhā sāntarhitā ||
children.translated_text: That beautiful radiance of complexion which they had disappeared.

children.text: andhakāraṃ loke prādurbhūtam ||
children.translated_text: Darkness appeared in the world.

children.text: dharmatā khalu gautamā andhakārasya loke prādurbhāvāt sūryācandramasor loke prādurbhāvo bhavati nakṣatrāṇām kṣaṇalavamuhūrtānāṃ rātriṃdivasānāṃ māsārdhamāsartusaṃvatsarāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, <s>Gautama</s>, it is the natural order that, with the appearance of darkness in the world, the sun and moon appear in the world, and the stars, moments, instants, muhūrtas, nights and days, months, half-months, seasons, and years appear in the world.

children.text: te tadbhakṣās tadāhārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as their food, they were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: teṣāṃ yo 'lpataram āhāram āharati sa varṇavān bhavati yaḥ prabhūtataram āhāram āharati sa durvarṇo bhavati ity āhāradvimātratāṃ pratītya varṇadvimātratā prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the one who took less food became fair in complexion, while the one who took more abundant food became ugly in complexion. Thus, dependent on the twofold measure of food, a twofold measure of complexion was perceived.

children.text: varṇadvimātratāyāṃ satyāṃ sattvaḥ sattvam avamanyate haṃbhoḥ sattva varṇavān ahaṃ durvarṇas tvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When there was a twofoldness of complexion, one being despised another being, saying, "Ho, being! I am fair in complexion; you are ugly in complexion."

children.text: teṣāṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ pṛthivīraso 'ntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While they were thus proud of complexion, because of their very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the earth-essence disappeared.

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīrase te sattvāḥ saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-essence had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur aho rasa aho rasa iti ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Ah, the taste! Ah, the taste!"

children.text: tadyathaitarhi manuṣyāḥ kiṃcid eva svādu subhojanaṃ bhuktvā tad eva purāṇam akṣarapadavyañjanam anusmaranta evam āhur aho rasa aho rasa iti ||
children.translated_text: Just as nowadays people, after eating some sweet and excellent food, recall that very old syllable, word, and expression and say, "Ah, the taste! Ah, the taste!"

children.text: evaṃ te sattvā antarhite gautamā pṛthivīrase saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: So too, <s>Gautama</s>, when the earth-essence had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur aho rasa aho rasa iti ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Ah, the taste! Ah, the taste!"

children.text: arthaṃ cāsya na jānanti ayam asya bhāṣitasyārtho 'yam asya bhāṣitasyārtha iti ||
children.translated_text: But they do not know its meaning, saying, "This is the meaning of that utterance; this is the meaning of that utterance."

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīrase teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ pṛthivīparpaṭakaḥ prādurbhūto varṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanna evaṃrūpo varṇena tadyathā karṇikārapuṣpam evaṃrūpo rasena tadyathā kṣaudramadhvaneḍakam ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-essence had disappeared, an earth-crust appeared for those beings, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste: in color it was like the flower of the karṇikāra, and in taste it was like pure honey.

children.text: te tadbhakṣās tadāhārāḥ dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as their food, they were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: teṣāṃ yo 'lpataram āhāram āharati sa varṇavān bhavati yaḥ prabhūtataram āhāram āharati sa durvarṇa ityāhāradvimātratāṃ pratītya varṇadvimātratā prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the one who took less food became fair in complexion, while the one who took more abundant food became ugly in complexion. Thus, dependent on the twofold measure of food, a twofold measure of complexion was perceived.

children.text: varṇadvimātratāyāṃ satyāṃ sattvaḥ sattvam avamanyate haṃbhoḥ sattva varṇavān aham asmi durvarṇas tvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When there was a twofoldness of complexion, one being despised another being, saying, "Ho, being! I am fair in complexion; you are ugly in complexion."

children.text: teṣāṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ pṛthivīparpaṭako 'ntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While they were thus proud of complexion, because of their very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the earth-crust disappeared.

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīparpaṭake te sattvāḥ saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-crust had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur aho bata aho bateti ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Ah indeed! Ah indeed!"

children.text: tadyathaitarhi manuṣyāḥ kenacid eva duḥkhadaurmanasyena spṛṣṭāḥ tāny eva purāṇāny akṣarapadavyañjanāny anuvyavaharanta evam āhur aho bata aho bateti ||
children.translated_text: Just as nowadays people, when touched by some suffering and dejection, use those same old syllables, words, and expressions and say, "Ah indeed! Ah indeed!"

children.text: evam eva te sattvā antarhite pṛthivīparpaṭake saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, when the earth-crust had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur aho bata aho bateti ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Ah indeed! Ah indeed!"

children.text: arthaṃ cāsya na jānanty ayam asya bhāṣitasyārtho 'yam asya bhāṣitasyārtha iti ||
children.translated_text: But they do not know its meaning, saying, "This is the meaning of that utterance; this is the meaning of that utterance."

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīparpaṭake teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ vanalatā prādurbhūtā varṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā evaṃrūpā varṇena tadyathā kadambakāpuṣpam evaṃrūpā rasena tadyathā kṣaudramadhvaneḍakam ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-crust had disappeared, a forest creeper appeared for those beings, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste: in color it was like the flower of the kadambaka, and in taste it was like pure honey.

children.text: te tadbhakṣās tadāhārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as their food, they were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: teṣāṃ yo 'lpataram āhāram āharati sa varṇavān bhavati yaḥ prabhūtam āhāram āharati sa durvarṇo bhavatīty āhāradvimātratāṃ pratītya varṇadvimātratā prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the one who took less food became fair in complexion, while the one who took much food became ugly in complexion. Thus, dependent on the twofold measure of food, a twofold measure of complexion was perceived.

children.text: varṇadvimātratāyāṃ satyāṃ sattvaḥ sattvam avamanyate haṃbhoḥ sattva varṇavān aham durvarṇas tvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When there was a twofoldness of complexion, one being despised another being, saying, "Ho, being! I am fair in complexion; you are ugly in complexion."

children.text: teṣāṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ vanalatā antarhitā ||
children.translated_text: While they were thus proud of complexion, because of their very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the forest creeper disappeared.

children.text: antarhitāyāṃ vanalatāyāṃ te sattvāḥ saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: When the forest creeper had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur apaihi purastād apaihi purastād iti evam eva te sattvā antarhitāyāṃ vanalatāyāṃ saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti klāmyanti paridevante ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Go away from before us! Go away from before us!" In just this way, when the forest creeper had disappeared, those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented.

children.text: evam āhur apaihi purastād apaihi purastād iti ||
children.translated_text: They said this: "Go away from before us! Go away from before us!"

children.text: arthaṃ cāsya na jānantyayam asya bhāṣitasyārtho 'yam asya bhāṣitasyārtha iti ||
children.translated_text: But they do not know its meaning, saying, "This is the meaning of that utterance; this is the meaning of that utterance."

children.text: antarhitāyāṃ gautamā vanalatāyāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānām akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliḥ prādurbhūta akaṇa atuṣaḥ śuddhaḥ śuciḥ caturaṅgulaḥ paryavanaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the forest creeper had disappeared, <s>Gautama</s>, rice with grain as its fruit, not ploughed or sown, appeared for those beings: without bran, without husk, pure, clean, and enclosed in four-inch grains.

children.text: sa sāyaṃ lūnaḥ kālyaṃ pakvaś ca bhavati prativirūḍhaś ca ||
children.translated_text: When it was cut in the evening, by morning it was ripe and had grown back.

children.text: kālyaṃ lūnaḥ sāyaṃ pakvaś ca bhavati prativirūḍhaś ca iti lūno lūnaḥ prativirohaty alūnaś ca prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: When it was cut in the morning, by evening it was ripe and had grown back. Thus, when cut again and again it grew back, and no cut place was perceived.

children.text: te tadbhakṣās tadāhārāḥ dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as their food, they were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: tataś ca te sattvā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ kavaḍīkārāhāropakrameṇa paribhuktavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those beings consumed the rice with grain as its fruit, not ploughed or sown, by the method of morsel-food.

children.text: tatas teṣām indriyanānātvaṃ prādurbhūtam ||
children.translated_text: Then diversity of faculties appeared among them.

children.text: ekeṣāṃ strīndriyam ekeṣāṃ puruṣendriyam ||
children.translated_text: In some there was the female faculty, and in some the male faculty.

children.text: tatra yeṣāṃ strīndriyaṃ yeṣāṃ ca puruṣendriyaṃ te 'nyonyaṃ cakṣuṣā cakṣur upanidhyāya paśyanti ||
children.translated_text: There, those in whom there was the female faculty and those in whom there was the male faculty looked at one another, placing eye upon eye.

children.text: ye yathā cakṣuṣā cakṣur upanidhyāya paśyanti tathā tathā saṃraktāḥ
children.translated_text: In just the way that they looked at one another, placing eye upon eye, in that same way they became impassioned.

children.text: yathā yathā saṃraktās tathā tathāvadīrṇā yathā yathāvadīrṇās tathā tathā vipratipannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In just the way that they became impassioned, in that same way they were inflamed; and in just the way that they were inflamed, in that same way they acted wrongly.

children.text: adrākṣur anye 'pi sattvāḥ sattvaṃ sattve vipratipannaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ pāṃsum api kṣipanti loṣṭam api śarkarā api kapālāny apyevaṃ cāhuḥ dhig grāmyasattva akāryakāraka dhig grāmyasattva akāryakāraka katham idānīṃ tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva sattvaṃ dūṣayasīti ||
children.translated_text: Other beings too saw a being acting wrongly with another being; and having seen it, they threw dust, clods, gravel, and potsherds, and said this: "Shame on you, coarse being, doer of what should not be done! Shame on you, coarse being, doer of what should not be done! How now, good being, do you defile a being?"

children.text: tadyathaitarhi manuṣyā vadhukāyām udvāhyamānāyāṃ cūrṇam api kṣipanti gandham api mālyam api vastrajālāny api kṣipanti ||
children.translated_text: Just as nowadays people, when a bride is being led away in marriage, throw powder, fragrance, garlands, and cloth nets.

children.text: evaṃ cāhuḥ sukhinī bhava vadhūke sukhinī bhava vadhūke iti ||
children.translated_text: And they say this: "Be happy, bride! Be happy, bride!"

children.text: evam eva te sattvāḥ sattvaṃ sattve vipratipannaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṃsum api kṣipanti loṣṭam api śarkarā api kapālāny api ||
children.translated_text: So too those beings, seeing a being acting wrongly with another being, threw dust, clods, gravel, and potsherds.

children.text: evaṃ cāhuḥ dhig grāmyasattva dhig grāmyasattva akāryakāraka katham idānīṃ tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva sattvaṃ dūṣayasīti iti hi gautamā yat pūrvam adharmasaṃmataṃ tad etarhi dharmasaṃmatam yat pūrvam avinayasaṃmataṃ tad etarhi vinayasaṃmatam yat pūrvaṃ garhyasaṃmataṃ tad etarhi praśasyasaṃmatam ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Shame on you, coarse being! Shame on you, coarse being, doer of what should not be done! How now, good being, do you defile a being?" Thus indeed, <s>Gautama</s>, what formerly was considered contrary to <s>dharma</s> is now considered in accord with <s>dharma</s>; what formerly was considered contrary to discipline is now considered in accord with discipline; what formerly was considered blameworthy is now considered praiseworthy.

children.text: te tam ekāham api pravāsayanti dvis triḥ saptāham api pravāsayanti ||
children.translated_text: They banish him for one day, or for two, three, even seven days.

children.text: yataś ca te sattvās tasmin pāpake asaddharme 'tyarthaṃ pātakavratam āpannās tatas te udyuktā agārāṇi māpayitum iha vayam akāryaṃ kariṣyāma iha vayam akāryaṃ kariṣyāma iti agāram agāram iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: And when those beings had entered into that evil, false dharma, a practice of very grave offense, they set themselves to building houses, saying, "Here we shall do what should not be done; here we shall do what should not be done." The designation "house, house" arose.

children.text: ayaṃ gautamā purāṇo 'graṇīr agāre karmāntānāṃ loke prādurbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Gautama</s>, was the ancient first appearance in the world of houses as places for activities.

children.text: yataś ca te dharmeṇa nādharmeṇa tatrāyaṃ dharmaḥ śreṣṭho jinendrāṇām te sāyaṃ ca sāyamāśārthinaḥ śālikāraṇāt samavasaranti prātaś ca prātarāśārthinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since this was by <s>dharma</s>, not by non-dharma, this <s>dharma</s> is supreme among the lordly victors: for the sake of rice they assemble in the evening, wanting an evening meal, and in the morning, wanting a morning meal.

children.text: athānyatareṇālasajātīyena sattvena sāyaṃprātikaḥ śālir ānītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain being of a lazy kind brought rice for both evening and morning.

children.text: athānyataraḥ sattvas taṃ sattvam idam avocat ehi tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva śālikāraṇāt samavasarāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Then another being said this to that being: "Come, good being, let us assemble for the sake of rice."

children.text: atha sa sattvas tam idam avocat pratijānīhi tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva svaṃ śālim ānīto mayā sāyaṃprātikaḥ śālir iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that being said this to him: "Know, good being, that I have brought my own rice; I have brought rice for evening and morning."

children.text: atha tasya sattvasyaitad abhavat etad bata sādhvetad bata suṣṭhu yannvahaṃ dvaiyahnikaṃ traiyahnikaṃ yāvat sāptāhikaṃ śālim ānayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then it occurred to that being: "Ah, this is good! Ah, this is excellent! What if I were to bring rice for two days, for three days, up to a week?"

children.text: sa dvaiyahnikaṃ yāvat sāptāhikaṃ śālim ānītavān ||
children.translated_text: He brought rice for two days, up to a week.

children.text: athānyataraḥ sattvas taṃ sattvam idam avocat ehi tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva śālikāraṇāt samavasarāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Then another being said this to that being: "Come, good being, let us assemble for the sake of rice."

children.text: atha sa sattvas taṃ sattvam idam avocat pratijānīhi tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva svaṃ śālim ānīto mayā sa dvaiyahnikaṃ traiyahnikaṃ yāvat sāptāhikaṃ śālir iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that being said this to him: "Know, good being, that I have brought my own rice; I have brought rice for two days, for three days, up to a week."

children.text: atha tasya sattvasyaitad abhavat etad bata sādhvetad bata suṣṭhu yannvardhamāsikaṃ māsikaṃ śālim ānayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that being thought this: "Ah, this would be good; ah, this would be excellent, if I were to bring rice for a half-month or a month."

children.text: so 'rdhamāsikaṃ māsikaṃ śālim ānītavān ||
children.translated_text: He brought rice for a half-month or a month.

children.text: yataś ca te sattvā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ saṃnidhīkāraparibhogena paribhuktās tatas tasya śāleḥ kaṇaś ca tuṣaś ca taṇḍulaṃ paryavanahyati lūno lūno na prativirohaty abalaś ca prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: And when those beings had consumed the naturally grown rice, whose fruit was grain, by storing it up and using it, then chaff and husk enclosed the grain of that rice; when cut, it did not grow back again, and it appeared weak.

children.text: ṣaṇḍavanaṣaṇḍeṣu vyavasthitaḥ śāliḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rice stood arranged in separate clumps and thickets.

children.text: atha te sattvāḥ saṃgamya samāgamya śocanti kāmyanti paridevante vayaṃ sma bhavantaḥ pūrvaṃ rūpiṇo bhavāmo manomayā avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ svayaṃprabhā vihāyasaṅgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥ prītyāhārāḥ dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those beings gathered and assembled, and they grieved, were distressed, and lamented: "Formerly, good sirs, we were corporeal, mind-made, unimpaired, with no deficient faculties, endowed with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, abiding in radiance, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, and we remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: teṣām asmākaṃ pṛthivīrasaḥ prādurbhūto varṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For us there appeared earth-essence, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste.

children.text: te vayaṃ pṛthivīrasaṃ kavaḍīkārāhāropakrameṇa paribhuktā yataś ca pṛthivīrasam kavaḍīkārahāropakrameṇa paribhuktā tato asmākam kharatvaṃ gurutvaṃ ca kāye 'vakrāntam yāsau śubhā varṇanibhā sāntarhitā andhakāraṃ loke prādurbhūtam ||
children.translated_text: We consumed the earth-essence by the procedure of morsel-food; and when we had consumed the earth-essence by the procedure of morsel-food, hardness and heaviness entered our bodies, that beautiful radiance of complexion disappeared, and darkness appeared in the world.

children.text: te vayaṃ tadbhakṣās tadāhārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as our food, we were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: teṣām asmākaṃ yo 'lpam āhāram āhṛtavān sa varṇavān bhavati yaḥ prabhūtam āhāram āhṛtavān sa durvarṇa ity āhāradvimātratāṃ pratītya varṇadvimātratā prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Among us, the one who took little food became fair in complexion, while the one who took abundant food became ugly in complexion; thus, dependent on the twofold measure of food, a twofold measure of complexion was perceived.

children.text: varṇadvimātratāyāṃ satyāṃ sattvaḥ sattvam avamanyate haṃbhoḥ sattva varṇavān ahaṃ durvarṇas tvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When there was a twofoldness of complexion, one being despised another being, saying, 'Ho, being! I am fair in complexion; you are ugly in complexion.'

children.text: teṣām asmākaṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ pṛthivīraso 'ntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While we were thus proud of complexion, because of our very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the earth-essence disappeared.

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīrase pṛthivīparpaṭakaḥ prādurbhūto varṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-essence had disappeared, an earth-crust appeared, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste.

children.text: teṣām asmākaṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ pṛthivīparpaṭako 'ntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While we were thus proud of complexion, because of our very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the earth-crust disappeared.

children.text: antarhite pṛthivīparpaṭake vanalatā prādurbhūtā varṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā ||
children.translated_text: When the earth-crust had disappeared, a forest creeper appeared, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste.

children.text: teṣām asmākaṃ varṇābhimānikānāṃ satāṃ teṣām eva pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samādānahetoḥ vanalatā antarhitā ||
children.translated_text: While we were thus proud of complexion, because of our very undertaking of evil, unwholesome dharmas, the forest creeper disappeared.

children.text: antarhitāyāṃ vanalatāyām akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliḥ prādurbhūtaḥ akaṇa atuṣaḥ śuddhaḥ śuciḥ caturaṅgulaḥ paryavanaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the forest creeper had disappeared, naturally grown rice, whose fruit was grain, appeared: without chaff, without husk, pure, clean, and enclosed in a measure of four finger-breadths.

children.text: sa sāyaṃ lūnaḥ kālyam pakvaś ca bhavati prativirūḍhaś ceti lūnaḥ lūnaḥ prativirohati alūnaś ca prajñāyate sma ||
children.translated_text: When it was cut in the evening, by morning it was ripe and had grown back; cut again and again, it grew back again, and it appeared as if uncut.

children.text: te vayaṃ tadbhakṣās tadāhārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Feeding on that and having that as our food, we were long-lived and remained for a long stretch of time.

children.text: yataḥ vayam akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphālaśāliṃ sannidhikāraparibhogena paribhuktavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when we consumed the naturally grown rice, whose fruit was grain, by storing it up and using it,

children.text: tato 'sya śāleḥ kuṇaś ca tuṣaś ca taṇḍulaṃ paryavanahyati ||
children.translated_text: then chaff and husk enclosed the grain of this rice.

children.text: lūno lūno na prativirohaty abalaś ca prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: When cut, it does not grow back again, and it appears weak.

children.text: ṣaṇḍavanaṣaṇḍeṣu vyavasthitaḥ śāliḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rice stands arranged in separate clumps and thickets.

children.text: yan nu vayaṃ saṃgamya samāgamya kṣetrāṇi māpayema sīmāṃ badhnīyāma maryādāṃ sthāpayema idaṃ tava idaṃ mameti te saṃgamya samāgamya kṣetrāṇi māpitavantaḥ sīmāṃ ca baddhavantaḥ maryādāṃ sthāpitavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What if we should gather and assemble, measure out fields, bind boundaries, and establish limits, saying, 'This is yours; this is mine'?" So they gathered and assembled, measured out fields, bound boundaries, and established limits.

children.text: ayaṃ gautamā purāṇo 'graṇīḥ maryādākarmāntānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This, <s>Gautama</s>, is the ancient first arising in the world of the business of boundaries and divisions.

children.text: tac ca dharmeṇa nādharmeṇa ||
children.translated_text: And that was according to <s>dharma</s> (right order), not according to non-<s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tatrāyaṃ dharmo dharmaḥ śreṣṭho jinendrāṇām ||
children.translated_text: There this <s>dharma</s> is <s>dharma</s>, the best among the Victorious Lords.

children.text: athānyatamaḥ sattvaḥ tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādatte ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain being, while standing in his own rice field, took another's rice that had not been given.

children.text: adrākṣīd anyataraḥ sattvaḥ taṃ sattvaṃ tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādadānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punas taṃ sattvam idam avocat kasmāt tvam bhoḥ sattva tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim ādatse gaccha bhos tvam sattva mā bhūya evaṃ kārṣir dvir api trir api sa sattvaḥ tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādatte ||
children.translated_text: Another being saw that being, while standing in his own rice field, taking another's rice that had not been given; and after seeing him, he said this to that being: "Why, good being, while standing in your own rice field, do you take another's rice? Go, good being; do not do such a thing again." But a second time and a third time that being, standing in his own rice field, took another's rice that had not been given.

children.text: adrākṣīt sa sattvaḥ taṃ sattvaṃ dvir api trir api tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādadānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punas taṃ sattvam idam avocat ||
children.translated_text: That being saw him a second time and a third time, while he was standing in his own rice field and taking another's rice that had not been given; and after seeing him, he again said this to that being:

children.text: kasmāt tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādatse ||
children.translated_text: "Why, good being, while standing in your own rice field, do you take another's rice that has not been given?"

children.text: sa tam ākarṣati parākarṣati yāvat parṣanmadhye 'py avatārayati ayaṃ bhavantaḥ sattvaḥ tiṣṭhati sve śālau parakīyaṃ śālim ādatta iti ||
children.translated_text: He pulled him and dragged him away, until he brought him down into the midst of the assembly, saying, "Good sirs, this being, while standing in his own rice field, takes another's rice."

children.text: atha te sattvās taṃ sattvam idam avocan kasmāt tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva tiṣṭhati sve śālau yāvat trir api parakīyaṃ śālim adattam ādatse gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva mā bhūya evaṃ kārṣir iti ||
children.translated_text: Then those beings said this to that being: "Why, good being, while standing in your own rice field, do you take another's rice, not given, even up to a third time? Go, good being; do not do such a thing again."

children.text: atha sa sattvas tān sattvān idam avocat anenāsmi bhavantaḥ sattvena śālikāraṇād ākṛṣṭaḥ parākṛṣṭo yāvat parṣanmadhye api avadhyāyitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that being said this to those beings: "Good sirs, because of rice I have been pulled about by this being, dragged away, and even accused in the midst of the assembly."

children.text: atha te sattvāḥ sattvam idam avocan kasmāt tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva sattvaṃ śālikāraṇād ākarṣasi parākarṣasi yāvat parṣanmadhye 'py avatarayasi gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva mā bhūya evaṃ kārṣīr iti ||
children.translated_text: Then those beings said this to that being: "Why, good being, because of rice do you pull a being about, drag him away, and even bring him down in the midst of the assembly? Go, good being; do not do such a thing again."

children.text: atha teṣāṃ sattvānām etad abhavat dṛśyante khalu bhavantaḥ śālikāraṇād ākarṣaṇam api parākarṣaṇam api yāvatparṣanmadhye 'py avatāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to those beings: "Good sirs, because of rice there are indeed seen pulling about, dragging away, and even bringing down in the midst of the assembly."

children.text: yan nu vayaṃ saṃgamya samāgamya yo 'smākaṃ sattvo 'bhirūpataraśca darśanīyataraś ca prāsādikataraś ca maheśākhyataraś ca taṃ vayaṃ kṣetrāṇām adhipatiṃ sthāpayema yo 'smākaṃ nigṛhītavyāṃśca nigrahīṣyati pragṛhītavyāṃś ca pragrahīṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "What if we should gather and assemble, and the being among us who is more handsome, more pleasing to see, more gracious, and more illustrious, him we should appoint as lord of the fields, one who will restrain those among us who should be restrained and will support those who should be supported?"

children.text: yac cāsmākaṃ kṣetrebhyaḥ sampatsyate tato 'smai dharmyāṃ kṣitim anupradāsyāma iti te saṃgamya samāgamya yas teṣāṃ sattvo 'bhirūpataraśca darśanīyataraś ca prāsādikataraś ca maheśākhyataraś ca taṃ kṣetrāṇām adhipatiṃ sthāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: "And from what is produced from our fields, we shall give him a rightful share." So they gathered and assembled, and the being among them who was more handsome, more pleasing to see, more gracious, and more illustrious, him they appointed as lord of the fields.

children.text: evaṃ cāhuḥ ehi tvaṃ bhoḥ sattva asmān nigṛhītavyāṃś ca nigṛhāṇa pragṛhītavyāṃś ca pragṛhāṇa yaccāsmākaṃ kṣetrebhyaḥ sampatsyate tatas te vayaṃ dharmyāṃ kṣitim anupradāsyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: And they said this: "Come, good being, restrain those among us who should be restrained, and support those who should be supported; and from what is produced from our fields, from that we shall give you a rightful share."

children.text: sa teṣāṃ nigṛhītavyāṃś ca nigṛhṇāti pragṛhītavyāṃś ca pragṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: He restrained those among them who were to be restrained and supported those who were to be supported.

children.text: yac ca teṣām kṣetrebhyaḥ sampadyate tato 'smai dharmyāṃ kṣitim anuprayacchanti mahājanena saṃmato mahāsaṃmata iti mahāsaṃmato mahāsaṃmata iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: And from what was produced from their fields, from that they gave him a rightful share. Since he was approved by the great multitude, the designation <s>Mahāsammata</s>, <s>Mahāsammata</s>, arose.

children.text: kṣetrāṇām adhipatiḥ kṣatāc ca trāyata iti kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriya iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: Since he was lord of the fields and protected from injury, the designation <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, arose.

children.text: dharmeṇa prajā rañjayati śīlavṛttasamudācāreṇa prajñāvṛttasamudācāreṇeti rājā rājeti saṃjñodapādi mahāsammatasya gautamā rājño manuṣyāṇāṃ sattvā sattvā iti saṃjñābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Since he delighted the subjects by <s>dharma</s> (right order), by conduct in morality and custom, and by conduct in wisdom and custom, the designation <s>rājā</s>, <s>rājā</s>, arose. For the beings who were the humans of <s>Mahāsammata</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> king, the designation "beings, beings" came to be.

children.text: mahāsammatasya gautamā rājño rocaḥ putraḥ rocasya rājño mānuṣyāṇām ehikā ehikā iti saṃjñodapādi rocasya gautamā kalyāṇaḥ putraḥ kalyāṇasya rājño mānuṣyāṇām tilakās tilakā iti saṃjñodapādi kalyāṇasya gautamā varakalyāṇaḥ putraḥ varakalyāṇasya gautamā rājño mānuṣyāṇām abhrakaṇṭhā abhrakaṇṭhā iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāsammata</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> king, had a son <s>Roca</s>. For the humans of king <s>Roca</s>, the designation <s>Ehika</s>, <s>Ehika</s>, arose. <s>Roca</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, had a son <s>Kalyāṇa</s>. For the humans of king <s>Kalyāṇa</s>, the designation <s>Tilaka</s>, <s>Tilaka</s>, arose. <s>Kalyāṇa</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, had a son <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>. For the humans of king <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, the designation <s>Abhrakaṇṭha</s>, <s>Abhrakaṇṭha</s>, arose.

children.text: varakalyāṇasya upoṣadhaḥ putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varakalyāṇa</s> had a son <s>Upoṣadha</s>.

children.text: upoṣadhasya gautamā rājño manuṣyāṇāṃ stālajaṅghā stālajaṅghā iti saṃjñābhūt ||
children.translated_text: For the humans of king <s>Upoṣadha</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, the designation <s>Stālajaṅgha</s>, <s>Stālajaṅgha</s>, came to be.

children.text: upoṣadhasya rājño mūrdhni piṭako jātaḥ mṛduḥ sumṛduḥ tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā na kadācid ābādhāṃ janayati ||
children.translated_text: On the head of king <s>Upoṣadha</s> a lump arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok; it never caused any pain.

children.text: paripākānvayāt sphuṭitaḥ kumāro jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ mūrdhnā jāto iti mūrdhnāto mūrdhnāta iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: As it matured, it split open, and a prince was born, handsome, pleasing to see, gracious, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Because he was born from the head, the designation <s>Mūrdhnāta</s>, <s>Mūrdhnāta</s>, arose.

children.text: jātamātraḥ kumāro 'ntaḥpuraṃ praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As soon as he was born, the prince was brought into the inner palace.

children.text: upoṣadhasya rājñaḥ ṣaṣṭistrīsahasrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Upoṣadha</s> had sixty thousand women.

children.text: sarvāsāṃ stanāḥ prasrutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The breasts of all of them flowed with milk.

children.text: ekaikā kathayati mān dhāpaya mān dhāpayeti māndhātā māndhāteti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: Each one said, "Let him suckle me; let him suckle me." Thus the designation <s>Māndhātā</s>, <s>Māndhātā</s>, arose.

children.text: yasmin samaye māndhātā rājā rājyaṃ kārayati tasmin samaye manuṣyāḥ cintakā abhūvan tulakā upaparīkṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the time when king <s>Māndhātā</s> ruled the kingdom, humans became thinkers, measurers, and investigators.

children.text: te cintayitvā tulayitvā upaparīkṣya pṛthakśilpasthānakarmasthānāni māpayantīti teṣāṃ manujā manujā iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: Because, after thinking, measuring, and investigating, they measured out the separate stations of crafts and occupations, the designation <s>manuja</s>, <s>manuja</s>, arose for them.

children.text: itīme gautamā ṣaḍrājāno 'mṛtāyuṣaś cābhūvann aparimitāyuṣaś ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Gautama</s>, these six kings were of deathless lifespan and of immeasurable lifespan.

children.text: antaroddānam ||
children.translated_text: Intermediate summary verse.

children.text: sattvā ehikās tilakā abhrakaṇṭhās tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The beings, the <s>Ehikas</s>, the <s>Tilakas</s>, and likewise the <s>Abhrakaṇṭhas</s>,

children.text: stālajaṅghāś ca manujā ṣaḍete uditāḥ padā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Stālajaṅghas</s> and the <s>Manujas</s>: these six are declared by name.

children.text: māndhātur gautamā rājño dakṣiṇe ūrau piṭako jāto mṛduḥ sumṛduḥ tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā sa na kāṃcid ābādhāṃ janayati ||
children.translated_text: On the right thigh of king <s>Māndhātā</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, a lump arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok; it caused no pain at all.

children.text: paripākānvayāt sphuṭitaḥ kumāro jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ dakṣiṇād ūror jātaś cāruś cārur iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: As it matured, it split open, and a prince was born, handsome, pleasing to see, gracious, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Because he was born from the right thigh and was beautiful, the designation <s>Cāru</s>, <s>Cāru</s>, arose.

children.text: maharddhikaḥ sa kumāro mahānubhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That prince had great supernormal power and great might.

children.text: athedānīṃ caturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān ||
children.translated_text: And now he exercised royal sovereignty and dominion over the four continents.

children.text: cāror gautamā vāme ūrau piṭako jātaḥ mṛduḥ sumṛdus tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā na kāṃcid ābādhāṃ janayati paripākānvayāt sphuṭitaḥ kumāro jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ vāmād ūror jātaḥ upacārur upacārur iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Cāru</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, on the left thigh a swelling arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok. It caused no pain at all. When, through maturation, it burst open, a boy was born, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Since he was born from the left thigh, the designation "<s>Upacāru</s>, <s>Upacāru</s>" arose.

children.text: maharddhikaḥ sa kumāro mahānubhāvo 'pīdānīṃ triṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān ||
children.translated_text: That prince was of great supernormal power and great might; and now he exercised sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over three continents.

children.text: upacāror gautamā rājño dakṣiṇe caraṇe piṭako jāto mṛduḥ sumṛdus tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā na kāṃcid ābādhāṃ janayati paripākānvayāt sphuṭitaḥ kumāro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ dakṣiṇāccaraṇājjātaḥ cārumāṃś cārumān iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: From King <s>Upacāru</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, on the right foot a swelling arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok. It caused no pain at all. When, through maturation, it burst open, a boy was born, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Since he was born from the right foot, the designation "<s>Cārumān</s>, <s>Cārumān</s>" arose.

children.text: maharddhikaḥ sa kumāro mahānubhāva ity apīdānīṃ dvayor dvīpayo rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān ||
children.translated_text: That prince was of great supernormal power and great might; and now he exercised sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over two continents.

children.text: cārumato gautamā rājño vāme caraṇe piṭako jātaḥ mṛduḥ sumṛdus tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā na kāṃcid ābādhāṃ janayati paripākānvayāt sphuṭitaḥ kumāro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ vāmāccaraṇājjāta upacārumān upacārumān iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: From King <s>Cārumat</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, on the left foot a swelling arose, soft, very soft, like a tuft of cotton or a tuft of kapok. It caused no pain at all. When, through maturation, it burst open, a boy was born, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Since he was born from the left foot, the designation "<s>Upacārumān</s>, <s>Upacārumān</s>" arose.

children.text: maharddhikaḥ sa kumāro mahānubhāvaḥ apīdānīṃ ekasmin dvīpe rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān ||
children.translated_text: That prince was of great supernormal power and great might; and now he exercised sovereignty, lordship, and dominion over one continent.

children.text: iti hi gautamā mahāsaṃmatasya rājño rocaḥ putraḥ rocasya kalyāṇaḥ kalyāṇasya varakalyāṇaḥ varakalyāṇasya upoṣadhaḥ upoṣadhasya māndhātā māndhātuś cāruḥ cāror upacāruḥ upacāroś cārumān cārumata upacārumān ruciḥ suruciḥ mucir mucilinda aṅga aṅgīratho bhṛṅgo bhagīrathaḥ sagaraḥ sāgaro mahāsāgaraḥ śakunir mahāśakuniḥ kuśa upakuśo mahākuśaḥ sudarśano mahāsudarśanaḥ praṇayo mahāpraṇayaḥ praṇādo mahāpraṇādaḥ prabhaṅkaraḥ pratāpavān merur merumān merumantaḥ arcir arciṣmān arciṣmantaḥ arciṣmantasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā potalake nagare ekaśatarājaśatam abhūt teṣām apaścimakaḥ arindamo nāma rājābhūd arīn damayatīty arindamaḥ arindama iti saṃjñā udapādi arindamasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā ayodhyāyāṃ catuḥpañcāśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ ajitañjayo nāma rājābhūd ajitaṃ jayatīty ajitaṃjayaḥ ajitaṃjaya iti saṃjñā udapādi ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Gautamā</s>, King <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s> had a son <s>Roca</s>; <s>Roca</s> had <s>Kalyāṇa</s>; <s>Kalyāṇa</s> had <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>; <s>Varakalyāṇa</s> had <s>Upoṣadha</s>; <s>Upoṣadha</s> had <s>Māndhātā</s>; from <s>Māndhātā</s> came <s>Cāru</s>; from <s>Cāru</s>, <s>Upacāru</s>; from <s>Upacāru</s>, <s>Cārumān</s>; from <s>Cārumat</s>, <s>Upacārumān</s>; then <s>Ruci</s>, <s>Suruci</s>, <s>Muci</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Aṅgīratha</s>, <s>Bhṛṅga</s>, <s>Bhagīratha</s>, <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Mahāsāgara</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Mahāśakuni</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Upakuśa</s>, <s>Mahākuśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, <s>Praṇaya</s>, <s>Mahāpraṇaya</s>, <s>Praṇāda</s>, <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, <s>Prabhaṅkara</s>, <s>Pratāpavān</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Merumān</s>, <s>Merumanta</s>, <s>Arci</s>, <s>Arciṣmān</s>, and <s>Arciṣmanta</s>. Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Arciṣmanta</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were one hundred and one hundred kings in the city of <s>Potalaka</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Arindama</s>. Because he subdued enemies, he was <s>Arindama</s>; the designation "<s>Arindama</s>" arose. Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Arindama</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were fifty-four thousand kings in <s>Ayodhyā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>. Because he conquered the unconquered, he was <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>; the designation "<s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>" arose.

children.text: ajitaṃjayasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā vārāṇasyāṃ triṣaṣṭī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako duṣprasaho nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were sixty-three thousand kings in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Duṣprasaha</s>.

children.text: duṣprasahasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kiṃpilye nagare caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako brahmadatto nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Duṣprasaha</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were eighty-four thousand kings in the city of <s>Kiṃpilya</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s>.

children.text: brahmadattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā hastināpure dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako hastidatto nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were thirty-two thousand kings in <s>Hastināpura</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Hastidatta</s>.

children.text: hastidattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā takṣaśilāyāṃ pañca rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ kālīśo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Hastidatta</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were five thousand kings in <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Kālīśa</s>.

children.text: kālīśasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā urasāyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako nagnajin nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Kālīśa</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were thirty-two thousand kings in the city of <s>Urasā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Nagnajit</s>.

children.text: nagnajito gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā ajitaṃjaye nagare dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako jayadatto nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Nagnajit</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were thirty-two thousand kings in the city of <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Jayadatta</s>.

children.text: jayadattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kanyakubjāyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako jayaseno nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Jayadatta</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were twelve thousand kings in the city of <s>Kanyakubjā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Jayasena</s>.

children.text: jayasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā campāyāṃ nagaryāṃ aṣṭādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako nāgadevo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Jayasena</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were eighteen thousand kings in the city of <s>Campā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Nāgadeva</s>.

children.text: nāgadevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā tālipye nagare pañcaviṃśatī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako naradevo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among the sons, grandsons, descendants, and further descendants of King <s>Nāgadeva</s>, <s>Gautamā</s>, there were twenty-five thousand kings in the city of <s>Tālipya</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Naradeva</s>.

children.text: naradevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā tāmaliptyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ sāgaradevo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of the royal <s>Naradeva</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were twelve thousand kings in the city of <s>Tāmalipti</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Sāgaradeva</s>.

children.text: sāgaradevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā dantapuryāṃ nagaryāṃ aṣṭādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ sumatir nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Sāgaradeva</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were eighteen thousand kings in the city of <s>Dantapura</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: sumater gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā rājagṛhe nagare pañcaviṃśatī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakas tamonudo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were twenty-five thousand kings in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Tamonuda</s>.

children.text: tamonudasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ekaśatarājaśatam abhūt teṣām apaścimako mahendraseno nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Tamonuda</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there were one hundred and one hundred kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Mahendrasena</s>.

children.text: mahendrasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kuśāvatyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ samudraseno nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Mahendrasena</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were eighty-four thousand kings in the city of <s>Kuśāvatī</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Samudrasena</s>.

children.text: samudrasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api potalake nagare rājasahasram abhūt teṣām apaścimakas tapaṃcaro nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Samudrasena</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Potalaka</s>, there were one thousand kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Tapaṃcara</s>.

children.text: tapaṃcarasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api kuśāvatyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako mahīmukho nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Tapaṃcara</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, there were eighty-four thousand kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Mahīmukha</s>.

children.text: mahīmukhasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ rājaśatasahasram abhūt teṣām apaścimako mahīpatir nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Mahīmukha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there were one hundred thousand kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Mahīpati</s>.

children.text: mahīpater gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api ayodhyāyāṃ nagaryāṃ śatasahasram abhūt teṣām apaścimako mahīdharo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Mahīpati</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, there were one hundred thousand kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Mahīdhara</s>.

children.text: mahīdharasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā mithilāyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimako mahādevo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Mahīdhara</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were eighty-four thousand kings in the city of <s>Mithilā</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: mahādevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api mithilāyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītimahādevasahasrāṇi rājarṣaya brahmacaryam acārṣuḥ teṣām apaścimako nimir nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Mithilā</s>, eighty-four thousand great <s>Mahādevas</s>, royal sages, practiced celibacy. The last of them was a king named <s>Nimi</s>.

children.text: nimer nimagno dṛḍhanemiḥ khanur upakhanuḥ khanumān khanumantaḥ sudṛśaḥ samadṛśaḥ śrutaseno dharmaseno vidito mahāvidito viditasena aśoko vigataśoko dṛḍhaseno jarāsandha dhundhumāraḥ aruṇo diśāṃpatir eṇḍaḥ saṃkakarakaḥ ānanda ādarśamukho janakaḥ saṃjanako janarṣabhaḥ annapānaḥ pracurānnapānaḥ ajito 'parājitaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ mahābalo mahābalavāhanaḥ sumatir dṛḍhavāhanaḥ śatadhanuḥ citradhanuḥ navatidhanuḥ vijitadhanur dṛḍhadhanur daśarathaḥ śataratho navatirathaḥ nararṣabhaḥ citraratho vicitraratho dṛḍharathaḥ dṛḍharathasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā sāṃkāśye nagare saptasaptatī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan teṣām apaścimakaḥ ambarīṣo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Nimi</s> came <s>Nimagna</s>, <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s>, <s>Khanu</s>, <s>Upakhanu</s>, <s>Khanumān</s>, <s>Khanumanta</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Samadṛśa</s>, <s>Śrutasena</s>, <s>Dharmasena</s>, <s>Vidita</s>, <s>Mahāvidita</s>, <s>Viditasena</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Vigataśoka</s>, <s>Dṛḍhasena</s>, <s>Jarāsandha</s>, <s>Dhundhumāra</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Diśāṃpati</s>, <s>Eṇḍa</s>, <s>Saṃkakaraka</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Ādarśamukha</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Saṃjanaka</s>, <s>Janarṣabha</s>, <s>Annapāna</s>, <s>Pracurānnapāna</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Aparājita</s>, <s>Pratiṣṭhita</s>, <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>, <s>Mahābala</s>, <s>Mahābalavāhana</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Dṛḍhavāhana</s>, <s>Śatadhanu</s>, <s>Citradhanu</s>, <s>Navatidhanu</s>, <s>Vijitadhanu</s>, <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>, <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Śataratha</s>, <s>Navatiratha</s>, <s>Nararṣabha</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>, <s>Vicitraratha</s>, and <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>. In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, there were seventy-seven thousand kings in the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>. The last of them was a king named <s>Ambarīṣa</s>.

children.text: ambarīṣasya gautamā rājñaḥ nāgasaṃpālaḥ putraḥ nāgasaṃpālasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ekaśataṃ rājaśatam abhūt teṣām apaścimako kṛkir nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, had a son, <s>Nāgasaṃpāla</s>. In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Nāgasaṃpāla</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there were one hundred groups of one hundred kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Kṛki</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena kāśyapo nāma śāstā loke utpannaḥ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān yasya antike bodhisattvo bhagavān āyatyāṃ bodhāya praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ caritvā tuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> had arisen in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One. In his presence the Blessed One, as a bodhisattva, made an aspiration for future awakening, practiced celibacy, and was reborn among the gods of the <s>Tuṣita</s> class.

children.text: kṛker gautamā rājñaḥ sujātaḥ putraḥ sujātasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api potalake nagare ekaśataṃ rājaśatam abhūt teṣām apaścimako karṇo nāma rājābhūt ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Kṛki</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, had a son, <s>Sujāta</s>. In the line of sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of king <s>Sujāta</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, once again in the city of <s>Potalaka</s>, there were one hundred groups of one hundred kings. The last of them was a king named <s>Karṇa</s>.

children.text: karṇasya gautamā rājño dvau gautamo bharadvājaś ca tayor gautamo naiṣkarmyābhinandī bharadvājo rājyābhinandī sa pitaraṃ paśyati dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayantaṃ sa saṃlakṣayati aham api pitur atyayād rājā bhaviṣyāmy aham api dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyāmi kim atra prāptakālam agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajiṣye iti viditvā yena karṇo rājā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Karṇa</s> had two sons, <s>Gautama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>. Of them, <s>Gautama</s> delighted in renunciation, while <s>Bharadvāja</s> delighted in kingship. He saw his father causing the kingdom to be ruled by both <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s>. He reflected, "After my father's passing I too shall become king. I too, having caused the kingdom to be ruled by both <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s>, shall have hell as my destination. What is now the proper time here? I shall go forth from the household into homelessness." Having understood this, he approached King <s>Karṇa</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya vijñāpayati tātānujānīhi māṃ pravrajāmi śraddhayā agārād anagārikām iti sa kathayati putra yasyārthe yajñā ijyante homā hūyante tapāṃsi tapyante tat tava karatalagataṃ rājyaṃ mamātyayād rājā bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he fell at his feet and petitioned him: "Father, permit me; with faith I shall go forth from the household into homelessness." He said, "Son, the kingdom, for the sake of which sacrifices are offered, oblations are poured, and austerities are practiced, is in the palm of your hand. After my passing you will become king.

children.text: kimarthaṃ pravrajasīti ||
children.translated_text: Why are you going forth?"

children.text: sa kathayati tāta na śakyaṃ mayā dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayituṃ tad anujānīhi pravrajāmīti tato rājñā avaśyaṃ nirbandhaṃ jñātvā anujñātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Father, I am not able to cause the kingdom to be ruled by both <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s>. Therefore permit me; I shall go forth." Then, knowing that his insistence was unavoidable, the king gave permission.

children.text: tena khalu samayena anyatamasminn āśramapade kṛṣṇadvaipāyano nāma ṛṣiḥ prativasati tato gautamaḥ kumāro rājñā samanujñāto hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajāto yena kṛṣṇadvaipāyano riṣis tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ upasaṃkramya vinīteryāpathapādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati pravrajyārthī pravrajāyasva mām iti ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time, in a certain hermitage there lived a sage named <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>. Then Prince <s>Gautama</s>, permitted by the king, delighted, satisfied, joyful, uplifted, and filled with gladness and happiness, approached the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>. Having approached, after making a respectful salutation and bowing at his feet, he said, "I seek going forth; cause me to go forth."

children.text: sa tena pravrajitaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano ṛṣiḥ phalamūlāṃbubhakṣaḥ tasyāpi gautama ṛṣiḥ gautama ṛṣiḥ iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: He was caused by him to go forth. The sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> lived on fruits, roots, and water. And he too came to be known by the designation, "the sage <s>Gautama</s>, the sage <s>Gautama</s>."

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena karṇo rājā kālagataḥ bharadvājakumāro rājyaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ pitryaṃ rājyaṃ kārayati yāvad apareṇa samayena gautamo ṛṣir upadhyāyāsya kathayati upādhyāya na śaknomi āraṇyakābhir oṣadhībhir yāpayituṃ grāmāntaṃ samavasarāmīti sa kathayati putra śobhanaṃ grāme vā araṇye vā prativasatā riṣiṇā sarvathā indriyāṇi rakṣitavyānīti gaccha tvaṃ potalasāmantakena śākhāparṇakuṭiṃ kṛtvā vāsaṃ kalpaya evam upādhyāya ity uktvā gautama riṣiḥ potalakasāmantakena śākhāparṇakuṭiṃ kṛtvā avasthitaḥ tena khalu samayena potalake nagare bhadrā nāma rūpājīvanī prativasati mṛṇālaś ca nāmnā dhūrtapuruṣaḥ tena vastrālaṃkāram anupreṣitaṃ paricāraṇāya sā tadvastrālaṃkāraṃ prāvṛtya samprasthitā anyatamaś ca puruṣaḥ pañcakārṣāpaṇaśatāny ādāyopasthitaḥ bhadre āgaccha paricāraya iti sā saṃlakṣayati yadi gamiṣyāmi pañcakārṣāpaṇaśatāni lapsye adākṣiṇyaṃ caitad gṛhāgataṃ pratyākhyāyānyatra gamanam iti tayā preṣyadārikābhihitā gaccha mṛṇālasya kathaya āryā kathayati na tāvad ahaṃ sajjā paścād āgamiṣyāmīti tayāpi tasya gatvārocitaṃ so 'pi puruṣo bahukaraṇīyaḥ sa tāṃ paricārya prathama eva yāme prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, King <s>Karṇa</s> died, and Prince <s>Bharadvāja</s> was established in royal sovereignty and overlordship; he ruled his father's kingdom. Then, after some time, the sage <s>Gautama</s> said to his preceptor, "Preceptor, I am not able to subsist on forest herbs. I will settle on the outskirts of a village." He said, "Son, good. Whether living in a village or in the forest, a sage must in every way guard the faculties. Go, make a hut of branches and leaves near <s>Potala</s>, and arrange a dwelling." "So be it, preceptor," he said; and the sage <s>Gautama</s> made a hut of branches and leaves near <s>Potalaka</s> and stayed there. Now at that time in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there lived a courtesan named <s>Bhadrā</s>, and also a rogue named <s>Mṛṇāla</s>. He sent clothing and ornaments for an assignation. She put on those clothes and ornaments and set out. But another man arrived with five hundred kārṣāpaṇas, saying, "<s>Bhadrā</s>, come, attend on me." She reflected, "If I go, I shall obtain five hundred kārṣāpaṇas; and it would be discourteous to reject one who has come to my house and go elsewhere." So she said to a servant girl, "Go and tell <s>Mṛṇāla</s>: 'The lady says, I am not yet ready; I shall come later.'" She went and informed him. That man also had many things to do; after enjoying her company, he departed in the very first watch of the night.

children.text: sā saṃlakṣayati mahatī velā vartate śakṣyāmy ahaṃ tasyāpi cittagrāhaṃ kartum iti tayā punar apy asau dārikābhihitā gaccha mṛṇālasyārocaya āryā sajjā saṃvṛttā kathaya katarad udyānam āgacchatv iti tayā tasmai gatvārocitaṃ sa kathayati kṣaṇena tavāryā sajjā kṣaṇenāsajjeti sā dārikā tasyāḥ sāntarā tayā samākhyātam āryaputra nāsāvasajjā kiṃ tarhi tayā tvadīyena vastrālaṃkāreṇānyena puruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ paricāritam iti tasya yattat kāmarāgaparyavasthānaṃ tad vigataṃ vyāpādaparyavasthānaṃ samutpannaṃ sa saṃjātāmarṣaḥ kathayati dārike gatvā bhadrāyāḥ kathaya mṛṇālaḥ kathayaty amukam udyānaṃ nirgaccheti tayā gatvā bhadrāyā ārocitaṃ tataḥ sā tad udyānaṃ nirgatā mṛṇālena dhūrtapuruṣeṇoktā yuktaṃ nāma tava madīyena vastrālaṃkāreṇānyena puruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ paricārayitum iti sā kathayati āryaputrāsty eva mamāparādhaḥ kiṃtu nityāparādho mātṛgrāmaḥ kṣamasveti tatas tena saṃjātāmarṣeṇa niṣkośam asiṃ kṛtvā jīvitād vyaparopitā tatas tayā preṣyadārikayā mahān kolāhalaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtaḥ āryā praghātitā āryā praghātiteti śrutvā samantāj janakāyaḥ pradhāvitaḥ yāvat tasminn evāśramapade gautamariṣiḥ prativasati tato 'sau mṛṇālo dhūrtapuruṣaḥ saṃtrasto rudhiramrakṣitam asiṃ gautamasya riṣeḥ purastācchorayitvā tasyaiva mahājanakāyasya madhyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ mahājanakāyaś ca rudhiramrakṣitam asiṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati anena pravrajitena bhadrā jīvitād vyaparopiteti ||
children.translated_text: She considered, "A long time has passed; I shall be able to win over his mind too." Then she again addressed that girl: "Go, inform <s>Mṛṇāla</s>: 'The noble lady has become ready. Say which garden he should come to.'" She went and told him. He said, "One moment your noble lady is ready, the next moment she is not ready." That girl had been bribed by her, and she reported to him, "Noble son, she is not unready. Rather, with your own clothes and ornaments she has been sporting with another man." Then that obsession of passion which he had disappeared, and an obsession of hostility arose. Becoming angry, he said, "Girl, go and tell <s>Bhadrā</s>: '<s>Mṛṇāla</s> says, go out to such-and-such a garden.'" She went and informed <s>Bhadrā</s>. Then <s>Bhadrā</s> went out to that garden. <s>Mṛṇāla</s>, the wicked man, said to her, "Is it proper for you to sport with another man using my clothes and ornaments?" She said, "Noble son, I do indeed have a fault; but women are always at fault. Forgive me." Then, becoming angry, he drew his sword from its sheath and deprived her of life. Then that servant-girl made a great tumult and cry: "The noble lady has been killed! The noble lady has been killed!" Hearing this, people ran from all around. Now in that very hermitage the sage <s>Gautama</s> was dwelling. Then that <s>Mṛṇāla</s>, the wicked man, terrified, threw the blood-stained sword before the sage <s>Gautama</s> and entered into the midst of that very great crowd. And the great crowd, seeing the blood-stained sword, said, "This renunciant has deprived <s>Bhadrā</s> of life."

children.text: tatas taṃ gautamariṣiṃ parivārya saṃjātāmarṣāḥ kathayanti bhoḥ pravrajita riṣidhvajaṃ dhārayasi īdṛśaṃ ca karma karoṣīti ||
children.translated_text: Then, surrounding that sage <s>Gautama</s>, they became angry and said, "Hey, renunciant, you bear the emblem of a sage, and yet you do such a deed!"

children.text: sa kathayati kiṃ kṛtaṃ te kathayanti bhadrayā te sārdhaṃ paricāritaṃ sā ca jīvitād vyaparopiteti sa kathayati śāntaṃ nāham asya karmaṇaḥ kārīti sa śāntavādy api tena mahājanakāyena paścādbāhugāḍhabandhanabaddho rājñe upanāmitaḥ devānena pravrajitena bhadrayā sārdhaṃ paricāritaṃ sā jīvitād vyaparopitā iti aparīkṣakā rājānaḥ kathayati yady evaṃ gacchata enaṃ śūle samāropayata parityakto 'yaṃ mayā pravrajita iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "What has been done?" They said, "You have sported with <s>Bhadrā</s>, and she has been deprived of life." He said, "Peace; I am not the doer of this deed." Although he spoke peacefully, that great crowd bound him tightly with his arms behind his back and presented him to the king: "Your Majesty, this renunciant sported with <s>Bhadrā</s>, and she has been deprived of life." Kings who do not investigate say, "If that is so, go, impale him on a stake. This renunciant has been abandoned by me."

children.text: tato 'sau pravrajitaḥ karavīramālāsaktakaṇṭhaguṇo nīlāṃbaravasanaiḥ puruṣair udyataśastraiḥ saṃparivārito rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu śravaṇāsukheṣv anuśrāvya dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa niṣkāsya jīvann eva śūle samāropitaḥ tasyāsāvupādhyāyaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ kālena kālaṃ tasyāśramapadam upasaṃkrāmati yāvad apareṇa samayenopasaṃkrāntaḥ na paśyati sa itaś cetaś ca samanveṣitum ārabdho yāvat paśyati śūlasamāropitaṃ sa bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ aśruparyākulekṣaṇaḥ karuṇadīnavilambitākṣaraṃ kathayati hā vatsa kim idaṃ so 'pi gadgadakaṇṭho marmavedanoparodhajanitaviṣādaḥ kathayaty upādhyāya karmāṇi kim anyad bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then that renunciant, with a garland of karavīra flowers fastened around his neck, surrounded by men wearing blue garments and holding raised weapons, was proclaimed in streets, roads, squares, and crossroads with unpleasant announcements; he was taken out through the southern city gate and impaled alive on a stake. His preceptor <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> used to come from time to time to that hermitage. After some time he came there and did not see him. He began to search here and there, until he saw him impaled on the stake. With his throat choked by tears and his eyes clouded with weeping, he said in syllables drawn out by compassion, misery, and grief, "Alas, child, what is this?" He too, with a choking throat and despair produced by the obstruction of pain in his vital parts, said, "Preceptor, deeds: what else could it be?"

children.text: sa kathayati vatsa nāsi kṣata upahato vā tāta kṣato 'haṃ kāyena no tu cittena vatsa kathaṃ jñāyate upādhyāya satyopayācanaṃ kariṣye śṛṇu yena satyena satyavacanena kṣato 'haṃ kāyena no tu cittena tena satyena satyavacanena yeyam upādhyāyasya kṛṣṇavarṇā chavir iyaṃ suvarṇavarṇā bhaved bhāvitādhyāśayo 'sau mahātmā vacanāvasānasamanantaram eva kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasya ṛṣeḥ kṛṣṇavarṇā chavir antarhitā suvarṇavarṇā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Child, are you not wounded or injured?" "Father, I am wounded in body, but not in mind." "Child, how is that known?" "Preceptor, I shall make an appeal to truth. Listen. By this truth and true statement, that I am wounded in body but not in mind, by that truth and true statement may this black-colored skin of the preceptor become golden-colored." That great-souled one had a cultivated intention. Immediately at the end of his words, the black-colored skin of the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> disappeared and became golden-colored.

children.text: sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanariṣiḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ saṃvṛtta iti ||
children.translated_text: A report spread through the neighboring region: "The sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> has become golden-colored."

children.translated_text: For him the designation "<s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>, <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>" arose. He was filled with the highest amazement. Then that sage <s>Gautama</s> said, "Preceptor, when I pass away from here, what will be my destination? What will be my rebirth? What will be my future course?"
