children.translated_text: He says, "Child, the brahmins say, 'There is no destiny for a man without a son.' Have you produced any offspring?" "Preceptor, I was only a boy, inexperienced in matters of women; urged by my father on account of the kingdom, I went forth. How could offspring arise for me?" "Child, if that is so, recollect the pleasures you formerly enjoyed." "Preceptor, now that I am struck by intense pain, while my vital points are being cut and my joints are coming loose, with my mind fixed only on death, how can there be recollection of pleasures formerly enjoyed?" That preceptor of his had attained the five superknowledges. By his miraculous power he created a great wind and rain. The drops of rain fell on his body. Then, from the touch of the cool water and wind, his pain was checked, and he began to remember the pleasures he had formerly enjoyed. Finally, from recollection of the passion of sexual union, two drops of semen mixed with blood fell. Four matters are inconceivable: reflection on the self, reflection on the world, reflection on the ripening of beings' actions, and reflection on the sphere of the buddhas. Those two drops of semen became two eggs. At the time of sunrise, ripened by the rays of the sun, they split open, and two princes were born. Not far from there was a sugarcane grove. They entered it. Then the rays of the sun became still more brilliant. The seer <s>Gautama</s>, scorched by the sun's rays, died. Then the seer <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s> arrived. He saw that <s>Gautama</s> had died. Near the stake he saw the eggs split open and the shells lying there. Following the trail here and there, he entered the sugarcane grove, until he saw the two princes. He set about considering, "Whose sons are these?" and saw that they were the sons of the seer <s>Gautama</s>. Then a still greater affection arose in him. He took them to the hermitage, gave them drink, nourished them, and raised them. He began to establish their names: "Since you were born at the time of sunrise, ripened by the rays of the sun, therefore you are of the solar lineage." Thus the designation <s>Sūryagotra</s>, <s>Sūryagotra</s>, arose. Since they were the sons of the seer <s>Gautama</s>, a second designation, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, arose. Since they had issued from his own limb, a third designation, <s>Āṅgīrasa</s>, <s>Āṅgīrasa</s>, arose. Since they were found in a sugarcane grove, a fourth designation, <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, arose. Then, at another time, king <s>Bharadvāja</s> died without a son. The ministers gathered and began to hold counsel: "Good sirs, whom shall we now consecrate as king?" Some said, "His brother, the seer <s>Gautama</s>, has gone forth among the seers. This kingdom has come down in his family line. Let us consecrate him." Having made this decision, they approached the seer <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>. They approached, fell at his feet, and said, "Great seer, where has <s>Gautama</s> gone?" He said, "He was killed by you yourselves." "Great seer, we do not even remember seeing him; how could we have killed him?" "I shall remind you." "Good." Then, when they had been reminded by him, they said, "Great seer, if that is so, enough of mentioning his name, for the proclamation of an evil deed should be avoided. What evil action did he do?" "This and that." "He was not a doer of evil action. Blameless and having done no harm, he was killed by you." "How?" Then he related in detail what had happened. They became dejected and said, "Great seer, if that is so, we are the doers of evil action, not he." While they were speaking in this way, those two boys approached the seer. The ministers said, "Great seer, whose boys are these?" He said, "They are that very man's sons." "How were they born, and what are their names?" He explained in detail their origin and names. When the ministers heard it, they were filled with the greatest wonder. Having asked the seer's permission, they consecrated the elder of the two princes with royal consecration. He too died without a son. Then the second, the younger one, was consecrated. For him the designation <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, arose. Among the sons, great-grandsons, grandsons, and further descendants of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> king, once again in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there were one hundred and one hundred <s>Ikṣvāku</s> kings.

children.translated_text: The last of them was an <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king named <s>Virūḍhaka</s>. King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, had four sons: <s>Ulkāmukha</s>, <s>Karakarṇī</s>, <s>Hastiniyaṃsa</s>, and <s>Nūpuraka</s>. Then, at another time, his chief queen passed away. He stood with his cheek resting on his hand, absorbed in thought. The ministers said, 'Why, Your Majesty, do you stand with your cheek on your hand, absorbed in thought?' He said, 'My chief queen has passed away; how should I not stand absorbed in thought?' 'Your Majesty, if that is so, why should a chief queen not be sought for Your Majesty? There are daughters of neighboring kings.' The king said, 'These princes desire the kingdom. With them present as rivals, who will give me his daughter?' 'Your Majesty, set your mind at ease; we shall search.' At length they found the daughter of a certain king, beautiful, lovely to behold, pleasing, and suitable for queenship. Having found her, they went to that king. By intermediaries the matter was reported to the king, and the king gave the order, 'Let them be summoned.' Then they were sent into the king's presence. They fell at his feet and sat down after preliminary conversation. When the occasion for discussion had come, they looked directly at the king and said, 'Your Majesty, welfare, welfare.' The king said, 'Gentlemen, what do you request?' 'The chief queen of <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, has passed away. We beg a maiden for that purpose.' The king said, 'Good; the suitor is suitable. But I shall give her on one condition: if a son is born to my daughter, he must establish him in royal power, sovereignty, and overlordship.' 'Your Majesty, let it be so. We shall go and inform our lord.' They went and reported to <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, exactly what had happened. The king said, 'Gentlemen, it is not fitting to reject the elder princes, who desire the kingdom, and establish the younger one.' 'Your Majesty, this matter is uncertain. Let the queen first be brought. Let Your Majesty sport with her, enjoy her, and be attended by her. It is not known whether she will bear a prince, or a princess, or whether she will be barren.' The king said, 'Gentlemen, if that is so, go; let there be acceptance.' They went and accepted her. The king married her with a great display of splendor, and she became beloved by the king. He sported with her, enjoyed her, and was attended by her. In time, as he sported, enjoyed himself, and was attended by her, the queen became pregnant. After eight or nine months had passed she gave birth. A boy was born, handsome, lovely to behold, and pleasing. At his birth they held a birth festival and set about assigning a name: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The ministers said, 'Your Majesty, since even before birth he has longed for the kingdom, let the boy's name be <s>Rājyābhinandī</s>.' The boy was entrusted to eight nurses, as before, and grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. The king did not establish him as crown prince. The king, his maternal grandfather, heard this and sent a messenger to him, writing harshly: 'You previously gave your consent. If you do as promised, all is well; if not, stand firm with whatever force, energy, and valor you have. I am coming, and I shall crush your realm.' That king possessed a great mass of force. Hearing this, <s>Virūḍhaka</s> was distressed. He assembled the ministers and asked, 'Gentlemen, that king has written such a thing to me. What should be done here?' They said, 'Your Majesty, let <s>Rājyābhinandī</s> be consecrated as crown prince.' He said, 'Gentlemen, it is not proper to reject the elder princes who desire the kingdom and consecrate the younger one.' They said, 'Your Majesty, that king has set out with a great army and vehicles. This situation exists: if he comes, he will certainly crush the realm. Let <s>Rājyābhinandī</s> be consecrated in royal power, sovereignty, and overlordship, and let the princes be banished from the kingdom.' The king said, 'Gentlemen, how can princes who have done no wrong and caused no harm be exiled?' 'Your Majesty, we ministers are intent on securing your welfare: we exile those who have done no wrong and caused no harm, and we establish one who is at fault and harmful.' The king, however, disregarded this and remained silent. The ministers gathered and began to confer among themselves: 'Gentlemen, a stratagem must be arranged by which the king will turn against the princes.' Then they had the garden cleaned and made bright and variegated, furnished with pots of fragrant incense, hung with garlands and strips of cloth, strewn with many flowers, and delightful. When that garden had been so prepared by the ministers, the princes saw it from afar and, being impetuous, set out toward the garden. The ministers, after arranging the garden's beauty, came out. The princes asked them, 'Whose garden is this?' They said, 'The king's.' The princes began to turn back. The ministers said, 'Princes, enter. Why do you turn back?' They said, 'It is the king's garden. How can we enter?' The ministers said, 'Either the king may sport there, or a prince may; what opposition is there in this?' They entered and began to sport. The ministers told the king, 'Your Majesty, the garden has been beautifully prepared; it is time for Your Majesty to see it.' The king set out. He heard a clamor in the garden, and, hearing the sound, asked the ministers again, 'Gentlemen, a clamor is heard in the garden. Who is staying there?' The ministers said, 'Your Majesty, the princes.' 'If that is so, the princes have been abandoned by me.' The ministers fell at his feet and said, 'Your Majesty, forgive the princes; do not abandon them.' The king said, 'Let it be so.' They then began to exile them. Falling at the king's feet, they said, 'Your Majesty, if this is so, be pleased to give an order that whatever retinue goes with us is not to be stopped.' The king gave the order. They set out. Since the people of the country were attached to them, a great mass of people set out with them. For seven days the city gate of <s>Potalaka</s> remained open as the crowd of people departed. The ministers reported to the king, 'Your Majesty, if the city gate is not closed, before long <s>Potalaka</s> will become uninhabited.' 'If that is so, close the gates.' Then the princes, taking their own sisters with them, gradually reached the side of the <s>Himavat</s>, the bank of the river <s>Bhagīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the seer <s>Kapila</s>. There they made huts of branches and leaves and arranged a dwelling. They made their livelihood by killing deer again and again, and three times a day they approached the hermitage of the seer <s>Kapila</s>. Swept away by the intoxication of fresh youth and greatly tormented by sensual passion, they became pale, very pale, and emaciated. Then, at another time, the seer <s>Kapila</s> saw them in such a condition and asked, 'Why are you pale and emaciated?' They said, 'Great seer, we are exceedingly tormented by sensual passion.' He said, 'Leaving aside your own full sisters, arrange to live with your half-sisters.' 'Is it permissible, great seer, for us to do this?' 'It is permissible, gentlemen, inasmuch as you are kṣatriyas fallen from kingship.' Then, taking the seer's word as authoritative, overcome by sensual passion and filled with delight and joy, they sported with their half-sisters, enjoyed them, and were attended by them. As they sported, enjoyed themselves, and were attended by those women, sons and daughters were born to them, and they grew up.

children.translated_text: The seer <s>Kapila</s>, because meditations are obstructed by sound, was not able to bring his mind to one-pointedness. He said, "Sirs, take notice: I shall go elsewhere." "Great seer, why are you unable to bring the mind to one-pointedness?" "Meditations are obstructed by sound." "Great seer, stay right here; we shall go elsewhere. But grant us this tract of land." "Sirs, very well." Those great-souled seers were accomplishers of desired wishes. Taking up a golden water-pot, they measured out the city in the form of a city by streams of falling water, and the seer <s>Kapila</s> gave up the site for their dwelling. Thus the designation <s>Kapilavastu</s>, <s>Kapilavastu</s>, arose. They grew there, and a great mass of people came into being. Because of crowding they could not increase further. Knowing their thought by means of their own thought, deities showed them another region. They went there and measured out a second city, <s>Devadriśa</s>, and the designation <s>Devadriśa</s>, <s>Devadriśa</s>, arose. Then they gathered and came together and began to converse: "Sirs, since we were banished because of taking wives equal to ourselves, no second wife equal to ourselves should be taken by any of us. Satisfaction must be had with one alone." Thus they marry only one suitable wife, not a second. Then, after some time, King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, remembering his beloved sons, addressed his ministers: "Ho, village-headmen, where are the princes now?" They reported the matter to him in detail: "Your Majesty, because of a certain affair they were banished. Taking their own sisters, they departed from here, and along the side of the Himālaya, on the bank of the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the seer <s>Kapila</s>, they have made their dwelling. Having rejected their own full sisters, they sport, enjoy themselves, and consort with their half-sisters. As they sported, enjoyed themselves, and consorted, sons and daughters were born to them." "Is it possible, village-headmen, for the princes to act in this way?" "Your Majesty, it is possible." Then <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, raising his body forward and stretching out his right arm, uttered an inspired exclamation: "Able indeed are the princes! Supremely able indeed are the princes!" Since a being of great renown had uttered the words, "The princes are <s>Śākyas</s>; the princes are supremely <s>Śākyas</s>," the designation <s>Śākya</s> arose.

children.translated_text: At another time <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, died. <s>Rājyābhinandin</s> was consecrated in the kingdom. He too died without a son. <s>Ulkāmukha</s> was established in royal sovereignty, lordship, and dominion. He too died without a son. <s>Karakarṇī</s> became king. He too died without a son. <s>Hastiniyaṃsa</s> became king. He too died without a son. <s>Nūpuraka</s> became king. His son was <s>Opuraka</s>; from <s>Opuraka</s> came <s>Gopuraka</s>. Among the sons, grandsons, grandsons' sons, and further descendants of King <s>Gopuraka Gautama</s>, there were fifty-five thousand kings in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. The last of them were <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Śataratha</s>, <s>Navatiratha</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>, <s>Vijitaratha</s>, <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, <s>Daśadhanu</s>, <s>Śatadhanu</s>, <s>Navatidhanu</s>, <s>Vijitadhanu</s>, <s>Citradhanu</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>. <s>Dṛḍhadhanu Gautama</s> had two sons, <s>Siṃhahanu</s> and <s>Siṃhanādin</s>. Indeed, among all <s>Gautamas</s> who are bowmen in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, <s>Siṃhahanu</s> is declared the foremost. <s>Siṃhahanu Gautama</s> had four sons: <s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Śuklodana</s>, <s>Droṇodana</s>, and <s>Amṛtodana</s>; and daughters: <s>Śuddhā</s>, <s>Śuklā</s>, <s>Droṇā</s>, and <s>Amṛtikā</s>. <s>Śuddhodana</s> had two sons, the Blessed One and the venerable <s>Nanda</s>. <s>Śuklodana</s> had two sons, the venerable <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Bhadraka</s> the Śākya king. <s>Droṇodana</s> had two sons, <s>Mahānāman</s> and the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>. <s>Amṛtodana</s> had two sons, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>. <s>Śuddhā</s> had a son <s>Suprabuddha</s>; <s>Śuklā</s> had a son <s>Mālī</s>; <s>Droṇā</s> had <s>Bhāddālī</s>; and <s>Amṛtikā</s> had <s>Śaivala</s>. The Blessed One had a son <s>Rāhula</s>. Thus, <s>Gautamā</s>, the lineage of <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s> was established in <s>Rāhula</s>. The cord leading to existence has been cut off, the round of birth has been exhausted; now there is no further rebirth.

children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing that the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s story had come to its conclusion, rose up and sat down. Having sat down, he addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: "Good, good, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>; good indeed, good indeed, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, that you speak before the monks a dharmic discourse concerning the ancient family lineage of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Again too, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, frequently speak a dharmic discourse concerning the ancient family lineage of the <s>Śākyas</s>. This will be for their welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long time." There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, learn the dharmic discourse concerning the ancient family lineage of the <s>Śākyas</s>, in order to retain it, teach it, and recite it. Why is that? Monks, the dharmic discourse concerning the ancient family lineage of the <s>Śākyas</s> is connected with meaning; it is connected with meaning and connected with the celibate life. It is fitting, monks, for a son of good family who has gone forth in faith to retain, teach, and recite the dharmic discourse concerning the ancient family lineage of the <s>Śākyas</s>." Then the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, rejoicing in and approving the Blessed One's speech, bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

vidhvastāḥ kṛtāḥ parituṣṭā smaḥ vada kumārasya kaṃ varam anuprayacchāmaḥ bhavantaḥ śākyaiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ na kenacid dve sadṛśe bhārye upasthāpayitavye iti deva kiṃ mucyatāṃ kriyākāraḥ sa kathayati sutarāṃ baddhavyo na moktavyaḥ kiṃtu kumārasyaikaṃ varam anuprayacchatha dvitīyāṃ sadṛśīṃ bhāryām upasthāpayituṃ deva śobhanam evaṃ kriyatāṃ tataḥ siṃhahanunā suprabuddhasya lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ avalokito mayā gaṇaḥ dvitīyāṃ duhitaram anupreṣayeti tena sāpi pañcaśataparivārā preṣitā śuddhodanena kumāreṇa dve api pariṇīte ||
children.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a king named <s>Siṃhahanu</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people. In the city of <s>Devadṛśa</s>, King <s>Suprabuddha</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people. King <s>Suprabuddha</s>'s chief queen, named <s>Lumbinī</s>, was beautiful, pleasing to see, gracious, and a beauty of the countryside. In <s>Devadṛśa</s> there lived a certain householder, wealthy, very rich, of great possessions, with broad and extensive property, endowed with wealth like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s and rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s wealth. His park was rich in flowers, rich in fruits, rich in rice, and filled with the calls of various birds. Because of its loveliness, the king would go there from time to time and enjoy pleasure and amusement together with his inner court. When <s>Lumbinī</s> saw it, longing arose in her. She said, "Your Majesty, grant me this park." The king said, "This park belongs to the householder. How can I grant it? But if you want a park, I shall have another, finer one made for your sake." Then King <s>Suprabuddha</s> had a park made for <s>Lumbinī</s>'s sake, finer than that one. It came to be called <s>Lumbinīvana</s>, <s>Lumbinīvana</s>. For a long time <s>Siṃhahanu</s> had this wish: "Ah, may a wheel-turning king arise in my family!" King <s>Suprabuddha</s> too had for a long time this wish: "Ah, may I have a marriage alliance with <s>Siṃhahanu</s>!" Then at another time, while he was sporting, delighting, and enjoying himself with the queen, after some time his wife became pregnant. After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth. A girl was born, beautiful, pleasing to see, gracious, complete in every major and minor limb. Because of the splendor of her beauty, King <s>Suprabuddha</s>, his inner court, and the people dwelling in <s>Devadṛśa</s> were filled with the greatest amazement and became uncertain in mind: "Is this a girl, or is this an illusion fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>?" When three sevens, twenty-one days, had passed since her birth, they held a great birth festival in full and began to establish a name: "What shall be the girl's name?" The ministers said, "Your Majesty, among the people dwelling in <s>Devadṛśa</s>, in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads, people are disputing. Some say, 'That is indeed a girl, produced as the maturation of former action, with such beauty of complexion and form.' Others say, 'She is not a girl. Rather, she is an illusion fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.' Therefore let the girl's name be <s>Māyā</s>." Her name was made <s>Māyā</s>. The girl <s>Māyā</s> was handed over to eight nurses, and, as before, she grew up until she became mature. She was predicted by the prognosticators: "She will give birth to a son endowed with many marks; he will become a king, a powerful wheel-turner." Again, while he was sporting, delighting, and enjoying himself, a daughter was born to him, shapely, pleasing to see, gracious, endowed with the highest fullness of complexion. At her birth that whole city was illuminated by a splendid radiance, and it was not possible in any way to describe the splendor of her beauty, as in <s>Māyā</s>'s case. For her too, when she was born, they held a great birth festival in full and began to establish a name: "What shall the girl's name be?" The ministers said, "Since the splendor of her beauty goes beyond <s>Māyā</s>, therefore let it be <s>Mahāmāyā</s>." She too was brought up and raised, and became mature. She was predicted by the prognosticators: "She will give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man; he will become a king, a wheel-turner." King <s>Suprabuddha</s> sent a messenger to <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: "Two daughters have been born, <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. Of these, one has been predicted: 'She will give birth to a son endowed with the marks; he will become a king, a powerful wheel-turner.' The second has been predicted: 'She will give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man; he will become a king, a wheel-turner.' Whichever of these two is desired for Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>, let her be brought." <s>Siṃhahanu</s> sent back this reply: "The prince has need of both, but two equal wives should not be provided for one man. Therefore let the one who has been predicted, 'She will give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man; he will become a king, a wheel-turner,' first be received. For the sake of the second I shall consult the assembly." So <s>Suprabuddha</s> sent her with an escort of five hundred. At that time enemies of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s>, had risen against them. The <s>Śākyas</s> gathered and approached King <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: "Your Majesty, we are being oppressed by the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s>. Provide assistance." He said, "Good sirs, I am old; I cannot fight with them." "Your Majesty, send Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>." "I shall send him on condition: if you grant the prince the boon he asks as he desires." They said, "Your Majesty, so be it; we shall grant it." The king gave him a fourfold army and sent Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>. By him those <s>Khaṣas</s> were struck down, beaten, and crushed. Then the <s>Śākyas</s>, pleased, approached King <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: "Your Majesty, the prince has struck down, beaten, and crushed the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s>. We are pleased. Say what boon we should grant the prince." "Good sirs, a rule has been made by the <s>Śākyas</s>: no one is to be provided with two equal wives." "Your Majesty, should the rule be released?" He said, "It should be bound still more firmly, not released. But grant the prince this one boon: to be provided with a second wife equal to the first." "Your Majesty, good; let this be done." Then <s>Siṃhahanu</s> sent a letter to <s>Suprabuddha</s>: "I have consulted the assembly. Send the second daughter." He sent her too with an escort of five hundred. Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s> married both of them.

sārdham upariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati dharmatā hy eṣā tuṣitabhavanastho bodhisattvaḥ pañcabhir avalokanair lokam avalokayati jātyavalokanena deśāvalokanena kālāvalokanena vaṃśāvalokanena stryavalokanena ca kena kāraṇena bodhisattvā jātyavalokanaṃ kurvanti tuṣitabhavanasthasya bodhisatvasyaivaṃ bhavati kīdṛśyāṃ jātau bodhisatvāḥ pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇantīti atonidānaṃ pare vaktāraḥ bodhisatvena garhaṇīyāyāṃ jātau pratisandhir gṛhīta iti tathā hi bodhisatvenānādikālīnam anākṣepasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtam upacitam avandhyaphaladharmadeśikā hi buddhā anuśrāvayati ito 'haṃ mārṣās tuṣitād devanikāyāccyutvā manuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ grahīṣyāmi rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāgramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau tasya putratvam adhigamya amṛtam adhigamiṣyāmi yo yuṣmākam amṛtenārthī jambūdvīpaḥ ṣaḍbhis tārkikaiḥ ṣaḍbhir ānuśravikaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ samāpattṛbhiḥ tatra ṣaṭ tārkikāḥ katame tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ maskarī gośāliputraḥ saṃjayī vairaṭṭīputraḥ ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ kakudaḥ kātyāyano nirgrantho jñātiputraḥ ṣaḍ ānuśravikāḥ katame tadyathā kūṭatāṇḍyo brāhmaṇaḥ śroṇatāṇḍyo brāhmaṇaḥ cogī brāhmaṇaḥ brāhmāyur brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇaḥ lohityaś ca brāhmaṇaḥ ṣaṭ pratipattāraḥ katame tadyathā udrako rāmaputraḥ arāḍaḥ kālāmaḥ subhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ saṃjayī māṇavaḥ asitariṣiḥ urubilvākāśyapaś ca jaṭilaḥ iha tu bodhisatvasya dvādaśayojanāni dharmaśravaṇārtham āsanaprajñaptiḥ prajñāpyate asmākaṃ caivaṃ bhavati yam asmākaṃ tuṣitabhavanastho bodhisatvo dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati taṃ vayaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tathā tathā pratipatsyāmahe yathāpi tad asmākaṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāyeti evam ukto bodhisatvaḥ tuṣitakāyikān devān idam avocat tena hi mārṣāḥ sarvavādyāni prahaṇyantām iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, King <s>Siṃhahanu</s> died, and in <s>Kapilavastu</s> King <s>Śuddhodana</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, secure, rich in food, and crowded with many people and human beings. Then, after some time, together with Queen <s>Mahāmāyādevī</s>, he went up to the upper terrace of the palace and amused himself, took pleasure, and enjoyed himself with music played where no men were present. For this is the regular order of things: while dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, a bodhisattva surveys the world by five inspections: inspection of birth, inspection of country, inspection of time, inspection of lineage, and inspection of the woman. For what reason do bodhisattvas inspect birth? While dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, this thought occurs to the bodhisattva: 'In what kind of birth do bodhisattvas take conception?' He sees: 'Either in a brahmin family or in a kṣatriya family. In some periods brahmins are regarded as the highest families; in some periods kṣatriyas are. But now kṣatriyas are regarded as the highest families. What if I were to take conception in a kṣatriya family? May others not, on this account, become speakers against me, saying, "The bodhisattva took conception in a blameworthy birth." For the bodhisattva has done and accumulated, from beginningless time, karma that does not lead to censure. The blessed buddhas are teachers of a dharma whose fruit is not barren.' For this reason bodhisattvas inspect birth. For what reason do bodhisattvas inspect country? This occurred to the bodhisattva: 'In what kind of country do bodhisattvas take conception?' He sees the country that is furnished with sugarcane, rice, garlands, cows, and buffaloes, crowded with hundreds of mendicants, free from bands of robbers, and inhabited by noble people. He thinks: 'This is the middle country, furnished with sugarcane, rice, garlands, cows, and buffaloes, crowded with hundreds of mendicants, free from bands of robbers, and inhabited by noble people. What if I were to take conception in the middle country? May others not, on this account, become speakers against me, saying, "The bodhisattva took conception in border provinces." For the bodhisattva has done and accumulated, from beginningless time, karma that does not lead to censure. The blessed buddhas are teachers of a dharma whose fruit is not barren.' For this reason bodhisattvas inspect country. For what reason do bodhisattvas inspect time? This occurred to the bodhisattva: 'At what kind of time do bodhisattvas take conception in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>?' They do not take conception when the population is in increase and people live for more than eighty thousand years. Nor do they take conception in a period of decline when human beings live for less than a hundred years. For what reason do bodhisattvas not take conception when human beings live for more than eighty thousand years? Human beings whose life span is eighty thousand years are hard to stir, hard to make understand, dull, of weak faculties, heedless, abounding in pleasures, and not fit vessels for the truths. And in decline, below a hundred years, the five degenerations become intense, namely the degeneration of life span, the degeneration of afflictions, the degeneration of beings, the degeneration of views, and the degeneration of the aeon. 'May others not, on this account, become speakers against me, saying, "The bodhisattva took conception at a time when the five degenerations were intense." For the bodhisattva has done and accumulated, from beginningless time, karma that does not lead to censure; and the blessed buddhas are teachers of a dharma whose fruit is not barren.' For this reason bodhisattvas inspect time. For what reason do they inspect family? The bodhisattva thinks: 'In what kind of family do bodhisattvas take conception?' He sees the family that is regarded as high and whose conduct is not reproached, as far back as the seventh generation on the mother's father's and father's father's sides. He thought: 'This <s>Śākya</s> lineage is regarded as a high family, going back as far as <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s>, and its conduct is not reproached. What if I were to take conception in the family of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>? May others not, on this account, become speakers against me, saying, "The bodhisattva took conception in an inferior family." For the bodhisattva has done and accumulated, from beginningless time, karma that does not lead to censure; and the blessed buddhas are teachers of a dharma whose fruit is not barren.' For this reason bodhisattvas inspect lineage. For what reason do bodhisattvas inspect the woman? The bodhisattva thinks: 'In the womb of what kind of woman do bodhisattvas take conception?' He sees the woman who is beautiful, virtuous, from a good family, noble, one who increases her family, who has made an aspiration before former buddhas, 'Ah, may I become the mother of a buddha,' who is able to bear the bodhisattva in her womb for ten months, and who does not neglect her own good. He thinks: 'This <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, as far back as the seventh generation on the mother's father's and father's father's sides, is of unreproached conduct, beautiful, virtuous, noble, one who increases her family, able to bear the bodhisattva in her womb for ten months, and not to neglect her own good. For <s>Mahāmāyā</s> has made a prior service and aspiration before former buddhas: "Ah, may I become the mother of a buddha." And may others not, on this account, become speakers against me, saying, "The bodhisattva took conception in the womb of a woman not endowed with the marks." For the bodhisattva has done and accumulated, from beginningless time, karma that does not lead to censure; and the blessed buddhas are teachers of a dharma whose fruit is not barren.' For this reason bodhisattvas inspect the woman. Then the bodhisattva, having surveyed the five inspections, made the announcement three times to the gods of the six desire realms: 'Friends, from here, having fallen from the divine company of <s>Tuṣita</s>, I shall take conception among human beings, in the womb of the chief queen of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having attained sonship to him, I shall attain the deathless. Whoever among you has need of the deathless, let him take conception among human beings, again in the middle country.' When this had been said, the gods belonging to the <s>Tuṣita</s> host said this to the bodhisattva: 'Bodhisattva, you should know this: the world now is full of strife and defilement; the generation of beings is cruel, and <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is made confused by six reasoners, six traditionalists, and six attainments-practitioners. Who are the six reasoners? They are <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośāliputra</s>, <s>Saṃjayī Vairaṭṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>. Who are the six traditionalists? They are the brahmin <s>Kūṭatāṇḍya</s>, the brahmin <s>Śroṇatāṇḍya</s>, the brahmin <s>Cogī</s>, the brahmin <s>Brāhmāyu</s>, the brahmin <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, and the brahmin <s>Lohitya</s>. Who are the six practitioners? They are <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>, <s>Arāḍa Kālāma</s>, the wandering ascetic <s>Subhadra</s>, the young man <s>Saṃjayī</s>, the seer <s>Asita</s>, and the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. But here, for the bodhisattva, a seat twelve yojanas wide is prepared for hearing the dharma. And we think: "The dharma that the bodhisattva dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode will teach us, having heard that dharma, we shall practice in such and such a way that it will be for our welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long night."' When this had been said, the bodhisattva said this to the gods belonging to the <s>Tuṣita</s> host: 'Then, friends, let all instruments be struck.'

children.text: tuṣitakāyikābhir devatābhiḥ sarvavādyāni prahatāni bodhisatvenāpi śaṅkham āpūryābhihitaṃ kataro 'tra mārṣāḥ odārikaḥ śabdaḥ śaṅkhaśabdo bhagavan yathāyaṃ mārṣāḥ śaṅkhaśabdaḥ sarvavādyāny abhibhūyāvasthitaḥ evam evāhaṃ jambūdvīpam avatīrya ṣaṭ tārkikān ṣaḍ ānuśravikān ṣaṭ ca pratipattṝn abhibhūyāmṛtam adhigamiṣyāmi amṛtena jagat saṃtarpayiṣyāmi anityatāśaṅkham āpūrayiṣyāmi śūnyatābherīṃ tāḍayiṣyāmīti nairātmyasiṃhanādaṃ nadiṣyāmīti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: The deities of the <s>Tuṣita</s> class struck all the musical instruments. The Bodhisattva too filled a conch and said, "Good sirs, which sound here is the more powerful?" "Blessed One, the sound of the conch." "Just as this conch-sound, good sirs, stands after overpowering all the musical instruments, so too, having descended to <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, I shall overpower the six reasoners, the six traditionalists, and the six practitioners, and I shall attain the deathless. With the deathless I shall satisfy the world. I shall fill the conch of impermanence; I shall beat the drum of emptiness; I shall roar the lion's roar of selflessness." Knowing this, he spoke a verse:

children.text: siṃhaikaḥ pramathati naikaśvāpadaughān vajraiko vilikhati naikaśṛṅgaśailān
children.translated_text: A single lion crushes many hosts of beasts; a single thunderbolt splits many horned mountains;

children.text: śakraiko vijayati naikadānavendrān sūryaiko vimathati naikam andhakāram ||
children.translated_text: a single <s>Śakra</s> conquers many lords of demons; a single sun dispels much darkness.

children.text: yo yuṣmākaṃ mārṣā amṛtenārthī sa madhyadeśe pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇātu ṣaṭsu mahānagareṣv iryatha śakrasya devendrasyaitad abhavat ayaṃ bodhisatvo bhagavān mahāmāyāyāḥ devyāḥ kukṣau pratisandhiṃ grahītukāmaḥ yannv aham asyā ojopasaṃhāraṃ kuryāṃ kukṣiṃ ca viśodhayeyam iti viditvā śakreṇa devānām indreṇa mahāmāyāyā devyāḥ ojopasaṃhāraṃ kṛtavān kukṣiṃ ca śodhitavān tatas tuṣitabhavanastho bodhisatvaḥ pañcāvalokitāni vyavalokya ṣaṭ kāmāvacarān devāṃs trir anuśrāvya gajanidarśanena rātryā madhyame yāme mahāmāyāyā devyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ āha ca
children.translated_text: "Good sirs, whoever among you has need of the deathless, let him take rebirth in the Middle Country. Go into the six great cities." Then this thought occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "This Blessed Bodhisattva wishes to take rebirth in the womb of Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. What if I were to bring nourishment to her and purify her womb?" Knowing this, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, brought nourishment to Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s> and purified her womb. Then the Bodhisattva, dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, having examined the five examinations and having proclaimed three times to the six gods of the desire realm, entered the womb of Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s> in the middle watch of the night, with the appearance of an elephant. And it says:

children.text: jagatparitrāṇakṛtapratijño devān upāmantrya tataś cyuto 'sau
children.translated_text: He who had vowed to protect the world, having addressed the gods, then passed away from there;

children.text: ikṣvākuvaṃśe praviveśa kukṣim sandhyābhrarājīm iva bālasūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he entered a womb in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, like a young sun entering a bank of twilight clouds.

children.text: tathā hi mahāmāyā caturaḥ svapnān paśyati ṣaḍdanto me śveto hastināgaḥ kukṣiṃ bhittvā praviṣṭaḥ upari vihāyasā gacchāmi mahāśailaparvatam abhiruhāmi mahājanakāyo me praṇāmaṃ karotīti tayā rājñe śuddhodanāyārocitam rājñā amātyānām ājñā dattā bhavantaḥ āhūyantāṃ svapnādhyāyavidaḥ naimittikāś ca brāhmaṇā iti taiś ca svapnādhyāyavido naimittikāś ca brāhmaṇā āhūtāḥ tato rājñā teṣām svapnāni niveditāni te kathayanti deva yathā śāstre dṛṣṭaṃ putraṃ janayiṣyati dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam sa ced gṛhī agāram adhyāvatsyati rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī sa cet keśaśmaśrūṇy avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati tathāgato bhaviṣyaty arhan samyaksaṃbuddho vighuṣṭaśabdo loka iti
children.translated_text: Accordingly <s>Mahāmāyā</s> saw four dreams: "A white lordly elephant with six tusks entered me after splitting open my womb; I am going through the sky above; I am climbing a great rocky mountain; and a great crowd of people is bowing down to me." She reported this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. The king gave an order to his ministers: "Gentlemen, let brahmins who know dream-texts and prognosticators be summoned." Those brahmins who knew dream-texts and those prognosticators were summoned. Then the king informed them of the dreams. They said, "Your Majesty, as it is seen in the śāstra, she will give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. If he remains a householder and inhabits the house, he will become a king, a wheel-turner. But if, having shaved off hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and gone forth rightly and with faith from the household into homelessness, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, famed in the world."

children.text: antaroddānam
children.translated_text: Intermediate summary:

children.text: cyutir devaputro ratanam aṣṭāṅgaṃ śrāntavratamānasam ||
children.translated_text: The passing away, the divine son, the jewel, the eightfold, and the mind wearied by vows.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvas tuṣitād devanikāyāccyutvā mātuḥ kukṣim avakrānto 'tyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūt sarvaś cāyaṃ lokaḥ udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhās tamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasāv evaṃmaharddhikāv evaṃmahānubhāvāvābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā abhūvan tatra ye sattvā upapannās te svakam api bāhuṃ pragṛhītaṃ na paśyanti te tayā ābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvān dṛṣṭvā saṃjānate anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti
children.translated_text: It is the regular nature of things that at the time when the Bodhisattva, having passed away from the divine host of <s>Tuṣita</s>, entered his mother's womb, at that very time an exceedingly great earthquake occurred, and this whole world was filled with a noble radiance. Even those spaces between the worlds, blind and dark with the gloom of darkness, where these sun and moon, of such great power and such great majesty, do not cause light to be experienced, were at that time filled with a noble radiance. The beings who had been born there do not see even their own raised arm; but by that light, seeing one another, they recognized, "Other beings, sirs, have been born here too; other beings, sirs, have been born here too."

children.text: yathaiva megho vipulaḥ susaṃbhṛto bahūdako mārutavegapreritaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a vast cloud, well gathered, rich in water, driven on by the force of the wind,

children.text: tathopamaṃ kukṣim ivākraman muniścirād ghanaṃ sūrya ivābhyupāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so, in like manner, the sage entered the womb, like the sun arriving after a long time through dense cloud.

children.text: avabhāsayitveha diśaḥ samantataḥ pṛthak ca lokāntarikās tamovṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Having illuminated the regions here on every side, and separately the spaces between worlds covered in darkness,

children.text: yadākramat kukṣim atulyavikramastathā tadāsīd iyam atra dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: when he of incomparable valor entered the womb, such then was the regular nature of things in this matter.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kuksāv avakrāntaḥ tasmin samaye śakro devendrāś caturo devaputrān mātur ārakṣakān sthāpayaty asihastān prāsahastāṃś chaktihastān tomarahastān mā kaścid bodhisatvaṃ viheṭayiṣyati manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo veti dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo mātuḥ kukṣāv asthāt kośogata evāsthād amrakṣito garbhamalena juvramalena rudhiramalena anyatamānyatamena vāśucinā viprakṛtena tadyathā maṇiratnaṃ kāśikaratne upakṣiptaṃ naiva maṇiratnaṃ kāśīkaratnena lipyate nāpi kāśikaratnaṃ maṇiratnena evam eva yasmin samaye bodhisatvo mātuḥ kukṣāv asthāt kośogata evāsthād amrakṣito garbhamalena juvramalena rudhiramalena anyatamānyatamena vā aśucinā viprakṛtena tadyathā maṇiratnaṃ dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣāv asthāt tam enaṃ tasmin sasmaye mātā sarvam antaḥkukṣigataṃ paripūrṇaṃ paśyati tadyathā maṇir aṣṭāṅgo vaiḍūryaḥ śubhro jātimān accho viprasanno 'nāvilaḥ pañcaraṅgike sūtre 'rpitaḥ syāt tadythā nīle pīte lohite 'vadāte māñjiṣṭhe taṃ cakṣuṣmān puruṣo dṛṣṭvā jānīyād idaṃ sūtram ayaṃ maṇiḥ sūtre maṇir arpitaḥ evam eva bodhisatvo yasmin samaye mātuḥ kukṣāv asthāt tam enaṃ tasmin samaye mātā sarvam antaḥkukṣigataṃ paripūrṇaṃ paśyati dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣāv asthān nāsya tasmin samaye mātā śrāntakāyā vā 'bhūt klāntakāyā vā yaduta bodhisatvaṃ dhārayantī dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣāv asthāt tasmin samaye mātā yāvajjīvaṃ pañcavratapadāni samādattavatī yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātaṃ prahāyā prāṇātipātāt prativiratā adattādānam ahrahmacaryaṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāṃ prahāya surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāt prativiratā prāṇān ahantī nādattam ādadau mṛṣā nāvocat na madyalolupā 'bhūt abrahmacaryād viratā ca maithunāt siddhārthamātā iyam atra dharmatā dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣāv asthān nāsya mātā tasmin samaye puruṣeṣu mānasaṃ nibaddhavatī yaduta kāmopasaṃhitam na rajyate kleśeṣu na cāsyāḥ kāmahetoḥ paridahyate manaḥ na cāsya mātā puruṣeṣu mānasaṃ badhnāti kāmaguṇopasaṃhitam ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva, the Blessed One, has descended into his mother's womb, at that time <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, appoints four divine youths as guardians of his mother, holding swords in their hands, holding spears in their hands, holding lances in their hands, and holding javelins in their hands, thinking, "Let no one, whether human or non-human, harm the bodhisattva." It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva remained in his mother's womb, he remained as if enclosed in a casket, unsoiled by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of fever, by the impurity of blood, or by any other foul contamination, just as a jewel-gem placed upon a Kāśika cloth is not stained by the Kāśika cloth, nor is the Kāśika cloth stained by the jewel-gem. In just this way, at the time when the bodhisattva remained in his mother's womb, he remained as if enclosed in a casket, unsoiled by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of fever, by the impurity of blood, or by any other foul contamination, just like a jewel-gem. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva, the Blessed One, remained in his mother's womb, then at that time his mother saw him complete in every respect within her womb, just as an eight-faceted beryl jewel, fine, noble, clear, transparent, and without turbidity, might be strung on a five-colored thread, that is, blue, yellow, red, white, and madder-red, and a man with eyes, seeing it, would know, "This is the thread; this is the jewel; the jewel is strung on the thread." In just this way, at the time when the bodhisattva remained in his mother's womb, then at that time his mother saw him complete in every respect within her womb. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva, the Blessed One, remained in his mother's womb, at that time his mother was not weary in body or exhausted in body through carrying the bodhisattva. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva, the Blessed One, remained in his mother's womb, at that time his mother undertook the five articles of the vow for as long as she lived: for as long as she lived, having abandoned killing living beings, she abstained from killing living beings; having abandoned taking what was not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and occasions of heedlessness caused by liquor, maireya, and intoxicants, she abstained from occasions of heedlessness caused by liquor, maireya, and intoxicants. She did not kill living beings, did not take what was not given, did not speak falsely, was not greedy for intoxicating drink, and abstained from unchastity and from sexual intercourse. This is the regular nature of things here concerning <s>Siddhārthamātā</s>. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the bodhisattva, the Blessed One, remained in his mother's womb, at that time his mother did not fix her mind upon men in a way connected with desire. She was not attached among the defilements, nor was her mind burned on account of desire, nor did his mother fix her mind upon men in a way connected with sensual qualities.

children.text: atha mahāmāyāyā dohada utpannaḥ aho batāhaṃ caturbhyo mahāsmudrebhyaḥ pānīyaṃ pibeyam iti tayā rajñe śuddhodanāyārocitam rājñā śuddhodanena naimittikānāṃ niveditam kimarthaṃ devyā ayam evaṃrūpo dohada utpannaḥ naimittikair vyākṛtaṃ deva devī kumārāṃ janayiṣyati dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtamūrtiḥ pravrajitvā sakalaṃ jñeyārṇavaṃ pāsyati rājñābhihitam yady asyāḥ mahāsamudrāt pānīyaṃ dīyate kiṃ tat syāt vyaṅgaṃ putraṃ janayet rājñābhihitaṃ mama tāvat śuddhodanasyāvikalāṅgaḥ putro bhaviṣyatīti tena khalu samayena kapilavastuni raktākṣo nāma parivrājakas tiṣṭhati indrajāle kṛtāvī rājñā tasyāhūya niveditam tena tasyā upariprāsādatalagatāyā yāvac caturo mahāsamudrān darśayitvā pānīyaṃ dattam tasyā yo dohada utpannaḥ sa prativigataḥ punar apy asyā dohada utpannaḥ aho bata sarvabandhanamokṣaḥ kriyeteti rājñā sarvabandhanamokṣaḥ kṛta iti tasyā yo dohada utpannaḥ sa prativigataḥ punar apy asyā dohada utpannaḥ aho bata dānāni dīyeran puṇyāni kriyerann iti rājñā dānāni dattāni puṇyāni kṛtāni tasyā yo dohada utpannaḥ sa prativigataḥ punar apy asyā dohada utpannaḥ aho batāham udyānāni paśyeyam iti rājñā udyānāni darśitāni tasyā yo dohada utpannaḥ sa prativigataḥ punar apy asyā dohada utpannaḥ aho batāham udyāne tiṣṭheyam iti rājñaḥ suprabuddhasya lumbinī nāmodyānam tasya śuddhodanena rājñā sandiṣṭaṃ duhitā te udyānaṃ nirgantukāmā udyānaṃ śodhayeti tena pauruṣeyāṇāṃ ājñā dattā bhavanta udyānaṃ śodhayateti tair udyānaṃ śodhitam tataḥ sā paricārikāsahīyā nirgatā tatas tayā luṃbinīvane vicarantyā sapuṣpitaḥ aśokapādapo dṛṣṭaḥ sā tam avalokyāvasthitā prasavitukāmā ||
children.translated_text: Then a pregnancy craving arose in <s>Mahāmāyā</s>: "Ah, if only I might drink water from the four great oceans." She reported this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> informed the prognosticators: "Why has such a craving arisen in the queen?" The prognosticators declared, "Your Majesty, the queen will give birth to a prince whose body is adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Having gone forth, he will drink the whole ocean of things to be known." The king said, "If water from the great oceans is given to her, what would happen?" They said, "She would give birth to a son with a defective limb." The king said, "As for me, <s>Śuddhodana</s>, my son will be one whose limbs are not defective." Now at that time in <s>Kapilavastu</s> there lived a wandering ascetic named <s>Raktākṣa</s>, skilled in magic. The king summoned him and informed him. He showed her, as she stood on the upper terrace of the palace, the four great oceans, and gave her water. The craving that had arisen in her disappeared. Again another craving arose in her: "Ah, if only there might be release from all bonds." The king caused release from all bonds to be made, and the craving that had arisen in her disappeared. Again another craving arose in her: "Ah, if only gifts might be given and merits performed." The king gave gifts and performed meritorious acts, and the craving that had arisen in her disappeared. Again another craving arose in her: "Ah, if only I might see the parks." The king showed her the parks, and the craving that had arisen in her disappeared. Again another craving arose in her: "Ah, if only I might stay in a park." King <s>Suprabuddha</s> had a park named <s>Lumbinī</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent word to him: "Your daughter wishes to go out to the park. Have the park cleaned." He gave orders to the workers: "Sirs, clean the park." They cleaned the park. Then she went out, accompanied by her attendants. As she wandered in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, she saw an aśoka tree in blossom. Looking at it, she stood still, wishing to give birth.

children.text: śakro devendraḥ saṃlakṣayati bodhisatvamātā hrīmatī na śaknoti mahājanaparivṛtā prasavitum upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam iti tena tumulaṃ vātavarṣaṃ nirmitam tenāsau mahājanakāyaḥ samantād vidrutaḥ tataḥ śakro devendraḥ vṛddhadhātrīvarṇam ātmānām abhinirmāya mahāmāyāyāḥ purastād avasthitaḥ sā prasavitum ārabdhā bodhisatvo nirgacchaṃś chakreṇājinaśāṭikāyāṃ pratigṛhītaḥ sa garbhavāsapariklāntaḥ atha bodhisatvasyaitad abhavat madaprāpto 'yaṃ śakro bhaviṣyati mayā bodhisatvaḥ pratīcchita iti viditvā vajraśarīram ātmānam adhiṣṭhitaḥ śakro devendraḥ kaṃpayitum ārabdho bodhisatvenābhihitaḥ muñca muñca kauśika apaihi purastād iti yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān jātaḥ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūt pūrvavad yāvad anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ satvā upapannā anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ satvā upapannā iti dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣer niṣkrāntaḥ kośogata ivāsir niṣkrāntaḥ amrakṣito garbhamalena juvramalena rudhiramalenānyatamānyatamena vā aśucinā viprakṛtena dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bodhisatvo bhagavān mātuḥ kukṣer niṣkrānto nāsya tasmin samaye mātā niṣaṇṇā vā 'bhūn nipannā vā sthitaiva sā kṣatriyī kṣatriyaṃ prasūtā dharmatā khalu sāṃpratajāto bodhisatvaḥ saptapadāni prakrāntaḥ parigṛhīto na kenacit caturdiṣaṃ ca vyavalokayati vācaṃ ca bhāṣate iyaṃ pūrvā dik pūrvaṃgamo bhaviṣyāmi nirvāṇāya iyaṃ dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇīyo bhaviṣyāmi kṛtsnasya dharmatā khalu sāṃpratajātasya bodhisatvasya mātur janayitryāḥ purastān mahad udapānaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ vāriniṣyandi yato 'sya mātā udakenodakakāryam akārṣīt dharmatā khalu sāṃpratajātasya bodhisatvasya devatā antarikṣāt divyāny utpalāni kṣipanti padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkāny agarucūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tamālapatracūrṇāni divyāni ca māndāravāṇi puṣpāṇi kṣipanti divyāni ca vādyāni pravādayanti
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, considered: "The Bodhisattva's mother is modest; surrounded by a great crowd, she cannot give birth. A means must be arranged." He created a violent wind and rain. Because of it that great crowd of people scattered in all directions. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, created himself in the form of an old nurse and stood before <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. She began to give birth. As the Bodhisattva came forth, he was received by <s>Śakra</s> in an antelope-skin cloth. He was wearied by dwelling in the womb. Then this occurred to the Bodhisattva: "This must be an intoxicated <s>Śakra</s>, thinking, 'The Bodhisattva has been received by me.'" Knowing this, he resolved his body to be diamond-hard. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, began to tremble. The Bodhisattva said to him, "Release me, release me, <s>Kauśika</s>; move away from the front." At the time when the Bodhisattva, the Blessed One, was born, there was a great earthquake, as before, up to: "Other beings, sirs, have been born here too; other beings, sirs, have been born here too." It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the Bodhisattva, the Blessed One, came out from his mother's womb, he came out like a sword from a sheath, unsoiled by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of fever, by the impurity of blood, or by any other foul contamination. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the Bodhisattva, the Blessed One, came out from his mother's womb, his mother was then neither sitting nor lying down; that kṣatriya woman gave birth to the kṣatriya while standing. It is indeed the regular nature of things that the newly born Bodhisattva took seven steps, held by no one, looked around in the four directions, and spoke these words: "This is the eastern direction; I shall be foremost, for nirvāṇa. This is the southern direction; I shall be worthy of gifts from the whole world." It is indeed the regular nature of things that before the mother and birth-giver of the newly born Bodhisattva a great well appeared, flowing with water, from which his mother performed the necessary washing with water. It is indeed the regular nature of things that, when the Bodhisattva was newly born, deities threw down from the sky divine blue lotuses, lotuses, water lilies, white lotuses, powders of agarwood, tagara, sandalwood, and tamāla leaves, and divine māndārava flowers, and they played divine instruments.

children.text: antaroddānām
children.translated_text: Intermediate summary:

children.text: utpādakośasthitiḥ sapta padāni dve vāridhāre udapānaṃ devatā
children.translated_text: The arising, the sheath, the standing birth, the seven steps, the two streams of water, the well, and the deities.

children.text: yadā śākyamunir bodhisatvo jātaḥ tadā caturṇāṃ rājñāṃ putrā jātāḥ śrāvastyām arāḍabrahmadattasya putro jātaḥ arāḍabrahmadattasyaitad abhavat mama putrasya janmani prasannaḥ prasanna iva janapadaḥ khyāti tasmād bhavatv asya prasenajit iti nāma rājagṛhe nagare mahāpadmasya rājñaḥ putro jātaḥ tasyaitad abhavat mama putrasya janmani ādityabimbenevodayatā loko 'vabhāsitaḥ bimbāyāś ca putraḥ bhavatv asya bimbisāra iti nāma kauśāṃbyāṃ śatānīkasya rājñaḥ putro jātaḥ tasyaitad abhavat mama putrasya janmani ādityenevodayatā loko 'vabhāsitaḥ bhavatv asyodayana iti nāma ujjayanyāṃ nagaryām anantanemino rājñaḥ putro jātaḥ anantanemino rājña etad abhavat mama putrasya janmani pradyoteneva loko 'vabhāsitaḥ bhavatvasya pradyota iti nāma tacca naivam api sarvaṃ tad bodhisattvānubhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Śākyamuni</s> was born as the Bodhisattva, sons were born to four kings. In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a son was born to <s>Arāḍabrahmadatta</s>. <s>Arāḍabrahmadatta</s> thought, "At my son’s birth the country appears bright and joyful, as if delighted; therefore let his name be <s>Prasenajit</s>." In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a son was born to King <s>Mahāpadma</s>. He thought, "At my son’s birth the world has been illuminated as if by the rising orb of the sun; and he is the son of <s>Bimbā</s>. Therefore let his name be <s>Bimbisāra</s>." In <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, a son was born to King <s>Śatānīka</s>. He thought, "At my son’s birth the world has been illuminated as if by the rising sun; therefore let his name be <s>Udayana</s>." In the city of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, a son was born to King <s>Anantanemi</s>. King <s>Anantanemi</s> thought, "At my son’s birth the world has been illuminated as if by a blazing light; therefore let his name be <s>Pradyota</s>." Yet it was not really so in all these cases; all of it was due to the power of the Bodhisattva.
